column5: Item
column6: Key facts and evidence
column7: Literature status
column8: Research angle

column5: Size and recent trend of the NINI stock (Colombia, 2019–2026)
column6: 2.3–2.7 M NINIs aged 15–28 (21–24%, DANE broad definition): 24.2% Dec 2025–Feb 2026, ≈21% Jun–Aug 2026; COVID peak 33% May–Jul 2020; Dec–Feb quarter seasonally highest. Press figures to check against bulletins. [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/poblacion-de-ninis-bajo-en-casi-70-000-en-el-ultimo-ano-y-ahora-suman-2-67-millones-4372184); [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/negocios/ninis-colombia-a-la-baja-2026-OA42351249); [La FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/economia/ninis-en-colombia-subieron-al-33-entre-mayo-y-julio)
column7: Descriptive only (DANE monthly bulletin; no thematic DANE report)
column8: Is the 2024–2026 decline seasonal, compositional or real? Compare like-for-like rolling quarters and decompose the change by NINI type, using GEIH back-cast microdata.

column5: Jump in the NINI rate between ages 16 and 18 (Colombia, 1984–2024)
column6: Age effect rises ≈5% to 22% between 16 and 18 (seven cities); vocational upper-secondary graduation age 16 in Colombia vs 22 in OECD; immediate tertiary transition ≈40%; most Cartagena NINIs completed media académica, so graduates rather than dropouts. [BanRep](https://banrep.gov.co/es/publicaciones-investigaciones/borradores-economia/jovenes-estudian-trabajan-dinamica); [Planeación Cartagena](https://planeacion.cartagena.gov.co/sites/default/files/2025-12/04nini.pdf)
column7: Descriptive only (synthetic cohorts); no study anywhere follows graduates who finish before legal adulthood
column8: Is the jump a graduation-age artefact? Plot NINI by single year of age, sex and completed level, comparing graduates and dropouts of the same age, using GEIH and Saber 11 cohorts.
column9: PoC (Q2, sec. 2.1, 4); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F1)

column5: Gender paradox: two thirds of NINIs are women while women dominate tertiary education (Colombia, 2015–2026)
column6: 64–68% of NINIs are women (broad), 71% per PND 2018–2022; young women 2.1 times more likely to be NINI; 25% of young women vs 8% of men (2015–2018); female NINI associated with early union, children under 5 and domestic work. [OCDE](https://www.oecd.org/es/publications/igualdad-de-genero-en-colombia_82e9b4e2-es/full-report/component-4); [RePEc](https://ideas.repec.org/a/col/000416/017798.html)
column7: Correlational only (multinomial logits); composition vs care penalty never tested
column8: Composition or behaviour? Decompose the female NINI rate by income, education and motherhood, and compare women with and without children within groups, using GEIH, ENUT and ENDS.
column9: PoC (Q1, E4); Literatura sobre ninis (sec. 1, 5); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F2)

column5: Falling female-to-male NINI ratio (Colombia, 2016–2023)
column6: ILO: women/men ratio fell from 2.4 to 1.9 because women exited NINI status faster; original ILO report not located (nv). Regionally, NINI growth over two decades was driven by men (male ninis +46%). [OIT](https://www.ilo.org/es/resource/news/uno-de-cada-cinco-jovenes-en-colombia-ni-estudia-ni-trabaja-hay-dos-mujeres); [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/negocios/ninis-en-colombia-hay-dos-mujeres-por-cada-hombre-en-esa-condicion-oit-AL24493605); [WB blog](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/education/nini-youth-latin-america-out-school-and-misunderstood)
column7: Descriptive only (press summary of ILO)
column8: Women exiting or men entering? Decompose changes in female and male rates separately by age, motherhood and falling fertility, using GEIH 2016–2025 back-cast series.
column9: PoC (Q4); Literatura sobre ninis (sec. 2.7); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F5)

column5: Steep income gradient in NINI status (Colombia, seven cities, 1984–2024)
column6: NINI ≈5% in high-income vs ≈40% in low-income households; 60% of Latin American ninis come from poor or vulnerable households. Current household income omits the youth's own earnings, so the gradient is partly mechanical. [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/economia/jovenes-nini-en-colombia-que-dice-el-nuevo-estudio-del-banco-de-la-republica/); [OKR](https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/entities/publication/83e4ac1b-aa2f-5eb2-ad54-db1acdbb5200/full)
column7: Descriptive only; income quintiles endogenous
column8: How steep is the gradient net of reverse causality? Re-estimate using per-capita income excluding the youth, SISBEN score at 16 or parental education, with GEIH and SISBEN IV.
column9: PoC (sec. 4, Lasso limitation 6); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F3, H11)

column5: Stock persistence: cohort NINI share stays high after 18 (Colombia, 1984–2024)
column6: Cohort NINI share stays above 15% after the jump (female rate above 20% after 17), but synthetic cohorts show a share, not that the same people remain NINI. Abroad: many short spells plus a minority core (Italy: over 40% NEET 13+ of 48 months). [IDEAS](https://ideas.repec.org/p/bdr/borrec/1363.html); [UniTo](https://iris.unito.it/bitstream/2318/1690470/1/JYS%202019%20preprint.pdf)
column7: No individual-level flow evidence in Colombia; Evidence abroad: Contini et al. 2019
column8: How much is transitory vs persistent? Compare individual NINI-to-NINI rates in ELCA and PILA formal spells of Saber 11 cohorts (lower bound) with synthetic-cohort persistence, by sex.
column9: PoC (Q3, Lasso limitation 1); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F4)

column5: Flat NINI cohort effect despite rising schooling (Colombia, cohorts since early 1970s)
column6: Cohort effect for NINI stable because rising "only studies" offsets falling "only works"; female NINI falls across cohorts. In Latin America male ninis rose as young women improved, so a flat total may hide opposite sex trends. [BanRep](https://banrep.gov.co/es/publicaciones-investigaciones/borradores-economia/jovenes-estudian-trabajan-dinamica); [WB blog](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/education/nini-youth-latin-america-out-school-and-misunderstood)
column7: Descriptive only (age-period-cohort decomposition)
column8: Does the flat total hide offsetting trends? Re-run the age-period-cohort decomposition separately by sex and NINI type, under alternative normalisations, on spliced ENH–ECH–GEIH 1984–2024.

column5: Countercyclical NINI rate (Colombia, peaks 1999 and 2020)
column6: Period effect countercyclical, peaking in 1999 and 2020; ninis also anticyclical in Brazil (Ipea, press). Abroad, short-term persistence rose after the Great Recession, especially for men. [CEDEFOP](https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/being_neet_before_and_after_the_great_recession.pdf); [MoneyTimes](https://www.moneytimes.com.br/ipea-23-dos-jovens-brasileiros-nao-trabalham-e-nem-estudam/)
column7: Descriptive only (APC period effects; time-series correlations)
column8: Which component is cyclical? Split NINI into searching vs care types and regress each on city unemployment and Bartik demand shocks in pooled GEIH; only the searching (mostly male) group should respond.
column9: PoC (sec. 4); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F6, H1)

column5: High NINI rate relative to OECD peers (Colombia, 2022)
column6: 27.1% of ages 18–24 (EAG 2022), second behind Turkey (28.7%), OECD average ≈14%, 67% women; minimum wage above 85% of median vs ≈50% OECD; no large apprenticeship bridge. [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/globoeconomia/colombia-es-el-segundo-entre-los-paises-de-la-ocde-con-la-mayor-tasa-de-ninis-3479534); [OCDE](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2024/11/oecd-youth-policy-toolkit_7ae28a3d/workshop-schools-tools-for-peace-programme-colombia_d38b635d.html)
column7: No academic decomposition; weakest-evidenced fact
column8: Is the ranking real? Recompute OECD/SDG definitions from GEIH, compare with SEDLAC, and Oaxaca-Blinder-decompose the gap into age-at-graduation, care and searching components, using ENUT for care.
column9: PoC (Q5, gap 7); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 8); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F7)

column5: Definitional discrepancies across sources (Colombia, 2008–2026)
column6: Strict (inactive only) 13.8% vs DANE broad 22% in 2023; the ≈8 pp gap is almost all unemployed; female share 75%+ strict (nv) vs 64–68% broad; age bands 14–28, 15–28, 15–24, 18–24; coverage national vs 13 or 7 cities. [LEE](https://javeriana.edu.co/recursosdb/5581483/11594517/INFORME99-NINIS-LEE2024%28notaaclart%29.pdf); [ILO repository](https://researchrepository.ilo.org/esploro/outputs/encyclopediaEntry/What-does-NEETs-mean-and-why/995242608602676)
column7: Descriptive only; Evidence abroad: Elder 2015 (NLEET), Freire & Saboia 2021 (Brazil)
column8: Do gender and level gaps shrink once definitions are harmonised (E8)? Build a sensitivity table (broad vs strict, four age bands, national vs cities) and separate models for inactive and unemployed NINIs, GEIH 2022–2025.
column9: PoC (E8, Table 2); Literatura sobre ninis (sec. 4, gap 10); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (H11)

column5: Territorial and ethnic gradient (Colombia, 2013–2024)
column6: Bogotá 18.5% (Q1 2024) vs Cartagena 28.8% (2023) and 26.9% (2024); Valledupar and Riohacha reported highest; high rates in Vaupés, Amazonas, Arauca, Vichada, Putumayo; in Cali being Afro-Colombian lengthens youth unemployment. [Semana](https://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/valledupar-y-riohacha-las-ciudades-con-mas-ninis-en-colombia/202211/); [La FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/economia/la-generacion-nini-estudia-trabaja-radiografia-del-fenomeno-colombia); [Bogotá.gov.co](https://bogota.gov.co/mi-ciudad/desarrollo-economico/trabajo-en-bogota-quienes-son-los-nini-ni-estudian-ni-trabajan)
column7: Descriptive only; ethnicity and region covered only for Cali and Cartagena
column8: Why the territorial gradient? Relate municipal NINI rates by ethnicity (Census 2018) to shift-share labour-demand shocks, conflict and displacement, and early unions in the Caribbean, with GEIH for 23 cities.

column5: E1 Liquidity constraints on post-secondary entry (Colombia)
column6: Central bank paper's main, tentative interpretation. Jóvenes en Acción relaxed credit constraints for women and works for the poorest quintile, but no evidence links liquidity to the age-18 timing or the female composition. [JHR](https://jhr.uwpress.org/content/57/1/178); [J-PAL](https://povertyactionlab.org/node/1668)
column7: No causal study; little direct support
column8: Does NINI fall when household income rises at 16–18, mainly among low-SES graduates (not dropouts)? Use household income shocks and SISBEN transfer cut-offs, with GEIH, SPADIES and SISBEN.
column9: PoC (E1, sec. 7.2); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (sec. 3)

column5: E2 Low perceived returns or misinformation (Colombia)
column6: Strict NINIs: only 19% hold a professional degree vs 38% of other youth (LaboUR, press). Abroad, a returns-information RCT raised schooling 0.20–0.35 years, with no effect for the poorest. [Semana](https://www.semana.com/educacion/articulo/estudio-de-la-universidad-del-rosario-sobre-jovenes-ninis-en-colombia/533281); [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:oup:qjecon:v:125:y:2010:i:2:p:515-548.)
column7: No Colombian study; Evidence abroad: Jensen 2010 (Dominican Republic)
column8: Does NINI respond to local returns to tertiary education rather than income? Exploit city-level college premium over time, distance to tertiary supply and information interventions, with GEIH and SNIES.

column5: E3a Graduation-age waiting room and age-18 legal gate (Colombia)
column6: Grade 11 ends at 16–17; work at 15–17 needs an inspector permit and the cédula arrives at 18 (legal details nv). Abroad, employment reacts sharply to age-specific costs (Denmark −33% at 18); under-age bans bind in inspected jobs (Brazil). [LSE](https://eprints.lse.ac.uk/100800/1/rest_a_00825.pdf); [EconPapers](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:oup:wbecrv:v:35:y:2021:i:1:p:234-260.)
column7: No study anywhere; Evidence abroad: Kreiner et al. 2020 (mirror), Bargain & Boutin 2021
column8: Do youths who graduate older have shorter NINI spells? School-entry cut-off RD conditional on graduating, plus an 18th-birthday RD in formal entries, using SIMAT–Saber 11–SPADIES–PILA.
column9: PoC (Q2, E3, design table); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F1, H3)

column5: E1/E6 Admission-rationing waiting after graduation (Colombia)
column6: Graduates missing SENA or public-university cut-offs face a waiting period; Los Andes admission offer raises enrolment 13.8 pp but rejected applicants' outcomes unreported; in Sweden a two-year delay costs ≈40–50% of annual age-40 earnings. [Uniandes](https://Economia.Uniandes.Edu.co/sites/default/files/seminariocede/The-Returns-to-College-Quality.pdf); [IFAU](https://www.ifau.se/en/Research/Publications/Working-papers/2006/Mind-the-gap-Estimating-the-effects-of-postponing-higher-education/)
column7: No study of rejected applicants; Evidence abroad: Holmlund et al. 2008
column8: Are applicants just below admission cut-offs more often NINI 6–18 months later, especially under 18? Admission-cut-off RDs on UNAL, Univalle and SENA records linked to SPADIES and PILA.

column5: E4 Care, motherhood and early partnership (Colombia)
column6: ≈80% of female NINIs mainly in household chores (official, press); 1 in 5 Bogotá women 15–24 already a mother; Colombian menarche IV: teen motherhood lowers schooling, little labour effect after selection. Child-marriage ban, Law 2447 of 2025 (nv). [CAF](https://scioteca.caf.com/handle/123456789/1727); [Uniandes](https://www.uniandes.edu.co/es/noticias/millennials-in-bogot%C3%A1%3A-decisions-for-the-future)
column7: Correlational only plus one IV (Agüero 2021); Evidence abroad: Assaad et al. (MENA, marriage)
column8: Does NINI jump after first birth or union, or is it selection? Event studies around first birth and union in ELCA, and Agüero's menarche IV with disaggregated NINI and union as outcomes (ENDS; menarche item nv).
column9: PoC (E4, gap 2); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 2); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F2, H4)

column5: E4c Older-daughter substitution in home production (Colombia)
column6: Untested in Latin America. India NREGS: girls replaced mothers' domestic work; Rio daycare lottery raised employment of adolescent siblings; counter-evidence via maternal bargaining (Afridi et al.). [IDEAS](https://ideas.repec.org/a/uwp/jhriss/v56y2021i2p380-405.html); [NBER](https://www.nber.org/papers/w30653)
column7: No study in Latin America; Evidence abroad: Shah & Steinberg 2021 (India)
column8: Are childless female care NINIs concentrated in households with under-3 siblings, working mothers and no grandmother? GEIH roster with a shift-share female-demand IV and CDI rollout; triple difference daughters vs sons.

column5: E3g/E3h Minimum-wage bite and signalling for low-income youth (Colombia)
column6: Minimum wage above 85% of median vs ≈50% OECD; city Kaitz up to 87.3 (Santa Marta 2016); informality rises with bite, especially for youth; +16% in 2023 (nv). Skill-report RCT raised youth employment 17% (South Africa). [BanRep](https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstreams/86fda998-ed96-45f1-8c61-3601bb2169c0/download); [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:bdr:borrec:1104); [AEA](https://www.aeaweb.org/doi/10.1257/aer.20200961)
column7: Panel correlation on informality only (Arango et al. 2020); NINI margin untested
column8: Does NINI of low-education 18–24 cells rise more in high-Kaitz cities after large increases, and do SENA certificates pay more there? Card-style fraction-affected design with GEIH city-quarter data, PILA and SENA certification RD.
column9: PoC (E3, policy table); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F3, H6, H9)

column5: E3i/E3j Referral networks and spatial mismatch (Colombia)
column6: Personal contacts dominate job finding; low-income youth's contacts are other disadvantaged youth (Cali, GEIH 2008); wages +7% within 500 m of TransMilenio; transport-subsidy effects faded by four years in Addis Ababa. [CORE](https://core.ac.uk/download/427654573.pdf); [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:oup:restud:v:88:y:2021:i:3:p:1279-1310.)
column7: Descriptive only in Colombia; Evidence abroad: Beaman & Magruder 2012
column8: Does youth NINI fall when household members gain formal jobs and rise after parental mass layoffs? Use the GEIH household roster and PILA plant closures (family linkage feasibility nv).
column9: Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F3, H12, sec. 4)

column5: D1 Two populations: male churning searchers vs female care core (Colombia)
column6: Abroad, about 60% of Argentine NINIs who find a job enter informal jobs; Brazil's NEET pool is "constantly renewing itself"; Italy's long-term inactive are mostly older women with children. [UNLP](https://www.me.econo.unlp.edu.ar/wp-content/uploads/Tesis-Martinez-Lorena.pdf); [UFF](https://periodicos.uff.br/revistaeconomica/article/download/35035/24645)
column7: No Colombian flow data analysed; Evidence abroad: Contini et al. 2019, Martínez (UNLP)
column8: Is persistence low for male searchers and high for female care NINIs, and is only the searching group cyclical? Transition rates by typology N1–N6 in ELCA, GEIH retrospective items and PILA spells.

column5: D2 State dependence and long-run consequences of NINI spells (Colombia)
column6: Cohorts with higher NINI shares at 16–22 show lower employment (men) and less salaried work (women) at 36–42, an ecological result; female scarring may run through job quality; Finland: lagged NEET raises NEET ≈3 pp; Cartagena links exclusion to illegal activity. [IDEAS](https://ideas.repec.org/p/bdr/borrec/1363.html); [UTUPub](https://www.utupub.fi/handle/11111/51011)
column7: No individual-level scarring evidence with administrative data; Evidence abroad: Gregg 2001, Mussida & Sciulli 2023
column8: Does a NINI spell causally lower formal employment and wages and raise early fertility or crime? Instrument spells with municipal Bartik demand at 16–18; outcomes from PILA, birth records and police data.
column9: PoC (Q6, gap 3, Lasso limitation 2); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 3); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (D2, F4)

column5: D3 Negative selection behind the flat cohort effect (Colombia)
column6: Schooling expansion may have pulled the most employable non-students into school, lowering "only works" without changing NINI; Familias en Acción cut urban dropout 5.8 pp and raised male college 1.7 pp; selection logic established only for returns to schooling. [VoxDev](https://www.voxdev.org/topic/public-economics/long-term-effects-conditional-cash-transfer-programmes-evidence-colombia); [IZA DP 5295](https://repec.iza.org/dp5295.pdf)
column7: No NEET study anywhere; Evidence abroad: Carneiro & Lee 2011, Huang et al. 2019
column8: Does reweighting non-enrollees to fixed composition remove the "only works" decline? DiNardo–Fortin–Lemieux reweighting and Lee bounds on GEIH cohorts, with Familias en Acción, Ser Pilo Paga and Generación E as shifters and Saber 11 scores.
column9: Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F5, D3, H2)

column5: E3l Recession and COVID entry scarring (Colombia, 1999 and 2020 cohorts)
column6: Graduating in a recession cuts initial earnings ≈9% in Canada, more and longer for the less advantaged; Latin American unlucky cohorts scarred 10 years on; Bogotá youth unemployment 18.7% to 33.3% (2019–2020); Colombian downgrade margin likely informality (speculative). [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:aea:aejapp:v:4:y:2012:i:1:p:1-29); [AAEP](https://bd.aaep.org.ar/anales/works/works2011/Cruces.pdf)
column7: Descriptive only on COVID; Evidence abroad: Oreopoulos et al. 2012, Cruces et al. 2011
column8: Did 1999 and 2020 entrants suffer lasting NINI or informality? Regress outcomes at 22–30 on entry-year city unemployment (Bartik IV) and compare adjacent graduating cohorts, using GEIH/ECH and PILA.
column9: PoC (Q8); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 7); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F6, H7)

column5: E5 School quality and dropout (Colombia)
column6: Many NINIs are secondary graduates, pointing away from E5 for the 16–18 jump; earlier full-day schooling raised test scores ≈0.1 SD, nothing on dropout or NINI; in Chile full-day school rollout cut teen motherhood. [Planeación Cartagena](https://planeacion.cartagena.gov.co/sites/default/files/2025-12/04nini.pdf); [IZA](https://docs.iza.org/dp4553.pdf)
column7: No causal study with NINI outcome; Evidence abroad: Kruger & Berthelon 2011
column8: Is NINI concentrated among early leavers and responsive to school shocks? Compare graduates with dropouts and use staggered Jornada Única adoption (Law 1753 of 2015) by school, with SIMAT linked to GEIH and PILA.
column9: PoC (E5, policy table); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F1)

column5: E7 Discouragement, preferences and reservation wages (Colombia)
column6: Press: over half of strict NINIs do not want to find work (LEE 99); pandemic labour or mental-health problems associated with NINI (Cuadernos de Economía 2026, authors nv); remittances lower participation in poor Coffee Axis households; UK NEETs report more work commitment. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/finanzas/mas-de-la-mitad-de-los-ninis-en-colombia-no-quiere-encontrar-trabajo-609554); [Redalyc](https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/861/86120154005.pdf)
column7: Correlational only; weak fit (leisure technology contested abroad: Aguiar et al. 2021)
column8: Do inactive youth who want work but do not search respond to income, demand or supply shocks? Use GEIH reasons for not searching, shift-share remittance shocks and heterogeneity across shocks.
column9: PoC (E7); Literatura sobre ninis (sec. 1); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (H13, H14, sec. 4)

column5: Venezuelan migrant youth and NINI status (Colombia, 2017–2026)
column6: No study found; BanRep authors tentatively link the post-2017 stagnation of school attendance to Venezuelan migration. GEIH migration module since 2021 and Encuesta Pulso de la Migración available. Reference: Lasso-Valderrama & Vargas 2026, BanRep Borrador 1363.
column7: No study
column8: How do legal status, credential recognition and care burdens shape migrant and native NINI? Use regularisation timing and municipal arrival intensity with the GEIH migration module.

column5: Jóvenes en Acción SISBEN RD and Renta Joven (Colombia, 2012–2024)
column6: DPS Res. 01970 (Nov 2012): transfer conditional on SENA or tertiary enrolment for poor secondary graduates; replaced by Renta Joven on 1 Jan 2024. RD: eligibility raises SENA enrolment 8–13 pp (Gamboa 2021). Earlier lottery: women's earnings +19.6%. [J-PAL](https://povertyactionlab.org/node/1668)
column7: RD on enrolment only; NINI outcome not studied
column8: Does SISBEN eligibility reduce NINI status and raise formal work (E1, E6)? Extend the Gamboa 2021 RD at the SISBEN cut-off to NINI and PILA outcomes; municipal phase-in (nv).
column9: PoC (E1, E6, policy and design tables, Q10); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 4)

column5: Re-analysis of Jóvenes en Acción and Familias en Acción experiments (Colombia, 2005–)
column6: Jóvenes en Acción lottery (ages 18–25): formal-sector effects persist up to eight years; Familias en Acción in Medellín cut teen pregnancy 2.3 pp, male arrests 2.7 pp and male dropout 5.8 pp. Neither measures NINI. [EconPapers](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:aea:aejapp:v:3:y:2011:i:3:p:188-220); [IDEAS](https://ideas.repec.org/p/nbr/nberwo/29056.html)
column7: Causal on other outcomes; NINI never an outcome
column8: Cheapest contribution: re-analyse both randomisations with disaggregated NINI status (unemployed, care, disability, discouraged) as outcome, using original data linked to PILA.
column9: PoC (gap 8, design table); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 9)

column5: Repeal of the 5% repetition cap (Colombia, 2010)
column6: Decree 230 of 2002 required at least 95% promotion; Decree 1290 of 2009 removed the cap from the 2010 school year; retention raised same-year dropout, most at grades 9 and 11. Reference: Ferreira 2020 (PoC).
column7: Effect on dropout only; destination of dropouts (work vs NINI) unknown
column8: Do induced dropouts end up working or NINI (E5)? School-level DiD on the change in retention rates, following students through SIMAT–PILA, plus GEIH event-time plots around 2010.

column5: SENA articulation of upper secondary and SENA expansion (Colombia, 2002–2016)
column6: Double certification in grades 10–11 adopted school by school from the early 2000s (nv); Bogotá Media Fortalecida ≈85,000 students by 2015; SENA instructors rose from 6,166 to 18,688 (2003–2010). Reference: DNP evaluation (method unknown).
column7: No causal study found
column8: Does articulation or SENA supply lower graduates' NINI (E6)? Staggered DiD by school adoption on later SENA and tertiary enrolment (SPADIES), formal work (PILA) and NINI; municipal SENA supply series not yet located.

column5: Apprenticeship contract rules and 2025 reform (Colombia, 2002–2025)
column6: Law 789 of 2002: firms with 15+ workers must hire apprentices, stipend 75% or 100% of minimum wage; Law 2466 of 2025 makes apprenticeship a labour contract, monetisation at 1.5 minimum wages per missing apprentice; 392,056 apprentices in 2024, 379,800 in 2025 (disputed). Reference: Ospino 2018 (PoC).
column7: RD at the 15-worker threshold for firm outcomes only; nothing on NINI
column8: Did the 2025 reform change apprentice hiring and youth NINI (E3, E6)? Use the firm-size threshold, the unemployment-triggered stipend rule and the reform date, with PILA and GEIH.
column9: PoC (policy table); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F7)

column5: Military ID card (libreta militar) rules for men (Colombia, 2014–2017)
column6: Law 1738 of 2014, Law 1780 of 2016 art. 20 and Law 1861 of 2017 art. 42 relaxed the requirement for degrees and hiring; current legal status unverified (nv); conscripts likely outside the GEIH sample (speculative). [Javeriana](https://apidspace.javeriana.edu.co/server/api/core/bitstreams/7917b8f9-55ab-490c-9c7a-8a807af8d75d/content)
column7: Only a master's thesis (null employment effect, Torres 2020); Evidence abroad: Mouganie 2020
column8: Is the NINI jump at 18 larger for men, and did it shrink after the reforms (E3b)? Triple difference men vs women, 18–24 vs older, pre vs post 2014/2017, plus difference-in-discontinuities at 18, GEIH.
column9: PoC (E3, policy and design tables); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F1, H10)

column5: Youth hiring incentives (Colombia, Ley 1429, 2016 and 2021 schemes)
column6: Ley 1429 under-28 incentives: under 15% of eligible firms applied in first six months; Law 1780 of 2016 art. 7 waived family-fund contributions for new hires 18–28; Law 2155 of 2021 subsidy of 25% of minimum wage per additional young worker, until ≈2023 (nv). [IDEAS](https://ideas.repec.org/a/rel/journl/y2017v14n1p40-59.html); [Externado](https://www.uexternado.edu.co/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/articulo14.pdf)
column7: DiD with mixed effects for Ley 1429; 2016 and 2021 schemes not evaluated; Evidence abroad: Saez et al. 2019
column8: Do hiring incentives reduce NINI (E3)? Age discontinuities at 18 and 28/29, before vs after 2016 and 2021, with hires and separations in PILA and NINI status in GEIH.
column9: PoC (E3, policy table); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F6)

column5: Early-childhood centre (CDI, De Cero a Siempre) expansion (Colombia, 2011–2016)
column6: Rapid expansion of care places 2011–2013; Law 1804 of 2016. Medellín Buen Comienzo raised maternal participation 3–9 pp but barely employment; Chilean after-school care RCT raised maternal employment ≈5%. [BanRep](https://banrep.gov.co/es/borrador-882); [J-PAL](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/evaluation/impact-extending-childcare-female-labor-chile)
column7: Evaluation of child outcomes only; maternal labour only in a master's thesis
column8: Does childcare supply reduce young mothers' and older sisters' NINI (E4)? Staggered event study of place growth by municipality for women with vs without children 0–5, using GEIH and ENUT.
column9: PoC (Q1, E4, policy and design tables); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 2); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (H4, H5)

column5: Free schooling and free tertiary tuition reforms (Colombia, 2004–2023)
column6: Decree 4807 of 2011: free grades 0–11 from 2012 (Bogotá 2004 for poorest SISBEN level); Ser Pilo Paga 2014–2018 (Saber 11 and SISBEN cut-offs); Generación E 2019; Matrícula Cero 2020–21; Law 2307 of 2023 free public undergraduate tuition. Reference: Barrera 2007; Londoño 2020 (PoC).
column7: RD on enrolment for Bogotá and Ser Pilo Paga; national reforms not evaluated; no NINI outcome
column8: Does free tuition cut NINI among low-SES graduates (E1)? RD at Saber 11 and SISBEN cut-offs and timing of free tuition by university type, with SPADIES, PILA and GEIH.
column9: PoC (E1, E5, Q10, policy table); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 4)

column5: Jóvenes en Paz and Sacúdete (Colombia, 2022–2026)
column6: Jóvenes en Paz (Law 2294 of 2023 art. 348; Decree 1649 of 2023): up to COP 1 million per month for ages 14–28 in prioritised territories, target ≈100,000; Sacúdete state policy since Law 2231 of 2022, only coverage figures (6,700 youth in Cauca). [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/node/187020); [Ley 2231](https://leyonline.co/laws/ley-2231-de-2022/articulo-3o-enfoque-de-la)
column7: No evaluation found
column8: Do current youth transfers reduce NINI status? Use territorial prioritisation and eligibility rules (RD or DiD) with SISBEN, SIMAT, PILA and GEIH.
column9: PoC (Q10, gap 4, policy table); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 4)

column5: NINI typology (N1–N6) and care measurement (Colombia)
column6: Only two Colombian studies separate home-care from job-seeking NINIs, one uses ENUT, none uses ETET 2013–2015; "household chores" is self-reported without hours; only ≈3% of Latin American youth do no productive activity and have no disability. [BID](https://webimages.iadb.org/publications/spanish/document/Millennials-en-Am%C3%A9rica-Latina-y-el-Caribe-%C2%BFtrabajar-o-estudiar.pdf); [catálogo DANE](https://microdatos.dane.gov.co/index.php/catalog/518/related-materials)
column7: Descriptive only; Evidence abroad: Freire & Saboia 2021 (Brazil)
column8: How large is the truly disconnected residual? Build the N1–N6 typology sequentially from GEIH, validate the care group with ENUT hours and use ETET transition histories.
column9: PoC (sec. 3.3, Stage 1); Literatura sobre ninis (gap 10); Evidence on NEET mechanisms (F2, E8)

column5: Coverage and method limits of the central bank synthetic-cohort study (Colombia, 1984–2024)
column6: Seven cities only (17.2% vs 23% nationally; paper reports both 18.2% and 17.2% for 2024); APC results depend on Deaton normalisation; 36-observation aggregate regressions with implausible signs; no individual-level analysis; care not separated. [PDF](https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstreams/6d434bdb-0232-4035-b950-61c7782ef78e/download)
column7: Only pseudo-panel in Colombia; correlational
column8: Do its conclusions survive national coverage and alternative normalisations? Replicate the seven-city series, extend to 23 cities and national GEIH, and estimate individual-level models of NINI type with predetermined SES proxies.

column5: Survey comparability and classification rules (Colombia, 1984–2026)
column6: GEIH redesigned on the 2018 census frame, back-cast series from Oct 2022; earlier redesigns in 2000 and 2006, working age moved from 12+ to 15+; one hour of paid work counts as employed; SENA and non-formal training may not count as studying; 2018 census omission enters expansion factors. [DANE](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/investigaciones/boletines/ech/juventud/boletin_GEIH_juventud_feb22_abril22.pdf)
column7: Undocumented in the literature
column8: How sensitive are levels and trends to classification rules? Harmonise reasons-for-inactivity questions across questionnaires and recompute rates under alternative study, work and coverage rules, GEIH back-cast series.

column5: Thin and partly unverified Colombian literature base (Colombia, 2015–2026)
column6: About six microdata studies, all cross-sectional logit or probit; none found in core Colombian journals or CEDE and Fedesarrollo series; thesis repositories poorly covered; original ILO 2024 report, Bernal et al. 2019 technical document, LaboUR report and Cuadernos de Economía 2026 authors not located (nv). [UNAL](https://revistas.unal.edu.co/index.php/ceconomia/article/view/107273)
column7: Search not exhaustive; all entries search-engine only
column8: Is there unpublished Colombian evidence? Run systematic searches in Google Scholar, RePEc, CEDE, Fedesarrollo and university repositories, and read the full Borrador 1363 tables by sex and income.
column9: PoC (sec. 7, Next steps); Literatura sobre ninis (sec. 0, 6)

column5: Post-COVID fertility collapse that stalls in 2026 (Colombia, 2022-2026)
column6: DANE TFR 1.4 (2022) → 1.0 (2025pr); births 453,901 in 2024 (−12.0%), −33% in a decade; births +1.5% in Jan-Jul 2026. [DANE](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/operaciones/EEVV/2026/20-mar-2026/cp-EEVV-Defunciones-IIsem2025pr.pdf); [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/nacimientos-en-colombia-cayeron-14-en-2024-y-33-en-ultima-decada/); [La FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/sociedad/nacimientos-defunciones-colombia-2026-411916)
column7: Partial causal (one margin only): PEP regularization cut migrant fertility (Amuedo-Dorantes, Ibáñez, Rozo & Traettino, EDCC 2025); otherwise Descriptive/Speculation
column8: Postponement vs migrant composition vs post-C-055 abortion: decompose EEVV births by age, parity, nationality and department (Cabella-style) with shift-share migrant stocks, then check levels against ENDS 2025 TFR.

column5: Adolescent fertility rises then halves (Colombia, 1990-2024)
column6: Ages 15-19: 70 (1990) → 90 (2005) per 1,000, urban-driven; 66.1 (2015) → 30.3 (2024), or ~32.3 per DANE. [Center for Reproductive Rights/ENDS](https://reproductiverights.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/sl_colombia_eng2006.pdf); [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/nacimientos-en-colombia-cayeron-14-en-2024-y-33-en-ultima-decada/); [Portafolio/DANE](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/numeros-historicos-la-principal-razon-de-la-caida-de-la-fecundidad-en-colombia-626640)
column7: Partial causal (earlier period): full-day schooling −0.6 pp (Borrero, CEDE 2017); otherwise Descriptive
column8: Displacement to urban peripheries (rise) vs LARC, Jornada Única and 4G (fall): staggered event studies on a municipal EEVV panel since 1998 with RUV, Jornada Única and 4G rollout dates.

column5: True fertility and population: DANE vs UN, 2018 census omission (Colombia, 2005-2023)
column6: 2023 TFR: World Bank 1.645 vs DANE 1.2; 2018 census omitted 8.5% (15% rural dispersed) vs 4.2% in 2005; implausible municipal TFRs (Tarso 0.3). [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SPDYNTFRTINCOL); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/tasa-de-poblacion-omitida-en-el-censo-de-2018-fue-de-8-5-de-acuerdo-con-el-dane-2922041); [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/negocios/antioquia-nacimientos-fecundidad-cae-debajo-un-hijo-por-mujer-NI29474191)
column7: Speculation (institutional): uncorrected 2005-based projections; DANE-UN gap: None
column8: Inflated denominators vs lagging UN WPP assumptions: reconcile EEVV 1985-2018 cohorts with the census and recompute TFR with SISBEN IV, BDUA and ENDS 2025 birth histories.

column5: Sub-1 fertility in Antioquia and Caldas, geographic inversion (Colombia, 2008-2025)
column6: Caldas TFR 0.7 (2024-25) vs Vaupés 2.0; Antioquia 1.9 (2008) → 0.9 (2024); Caldas births −19.3% vs −7.8% nationally (2015-21). [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/salud/nacimientos-y-decesos-en-colombia-tasas-de-fecundidad-siguen-en-descenso-segun-el-dane/); [El Colombiano, 26-Sep-2025](https://www.elcolombiano.com/negocios/antioquia-nacimientos-fecundidad-cae-debajo-un-hijo-por-mujer-NI29474191); [Caldata](https://caldata.caldas.gov.co/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Boletin-21-Natalidad-y-fecundidad-en-Caldas.pdf)
column7: Descriptive: coffee-region fertility study 1998-2018 (EconBiz); emigrant women have lower fertility (UAB)
column8: Denominator artefact vs selective emigration vs behaviour: TFR recomputed with SISBEN/BDUA, 2005 municipal emigration × coffee price, and IPUMS 1964/1973 to date the inversion.

column5: Female household headship nearly doubles, one-person households reach 20% (Colombia, 1993-2024)
column6: Female headship 24% (1993) → 40.7% (2018) → 46.5% (ECV 2024); one-person households 11.1% → 20.2%. [DANE](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/censos/presentaciones/jefes_hogar.pdf); [ECV 2024](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/operaciones/ECV/bol-ECV-2024.pdf); [El Tiempo](https://www.eltiempo.com/economia/sectores/que-implica-que-los-hogares-colombianos-sean-mas-pequenos-analisis-censo-2018-311776)
column7: Speculation: "empowerment" framing (DANE); academic causal work: None
column8: Reporting-norm change vs real household restructuring: share of female heads with a spouse present in IPUMS 1993/2005/2018, municipal male homicide, and staggered Familias en Acción entry (2001-07).

column5: Cohabitation boom with an "unchanged" social profile (Colombia, 1973-2010)
column6: Women 25-29 in cohabitation: 20% (1973) → 66% (2005), ~73.6% in ENDS 2010; 77% of separated people come from consensual unions. [Esteve et al. 2016](https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-31442-6_7); [Dialnet](https://dialnet.unirioja.es/descarga/articulo/7900883.pdf)
column7: Descriptive: Esteve, Lesthaeghe & López-Gay 2012 (catching-up of the educated, no economic correlation)
column8: Legal reforms (Ley 54/1990, 1992 divorce, survivor pensions; dates nv) vs wedding costs and informality: differential reform exposure and Bartik income shocks on registered marriages, using IPUMS, ENDS and notarial records.

column5: Older adults without pensions increasingly live alone (Colombia, c. 2018-2025)
column6: 29.5% of older adults have a pension, 19% receive Colombia Mayor; 43.8% of those aged 60-69 work; living alone is the most common old-age arrangement, 19.1% in 2018 (authorship nv). [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/especiales/economia-silver/politicas-de-envejecimiento-3687486); [El País Cali](https://www.elpais.com.co/economia/adultos-mayores-en-colombia-hoy-son-mas-activos-y-productivos.html); [Springer](https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s12062-022-09374-6)
column7: Descriptive (demographic studies only); economic: None
column8: Children's emigration vs Colombia Mayor income effect: age discontinuity and 2023-25 benefit changes in Colombia Mayor plus 2005-2018 municipal emigration, using ECV, GEIH and census.

column5: School enrollment falls faster than population while PISA-eligible 15-year-olds rise (Colombia, 2015-2025)
column6: 9,318,417 enrolled in 2025, −920k since 2015 (LEE: −696k over the decade); LEE says demography is "insufficient", 81% of the drop is public; OECD: PISA-eligible population rose 2018-2025. [Forbes](https://forbes.co/2026/05/12/actualidad/la-matricula-de-colegios-en-colombia-cae-a-93-millones-de-estudiantes-su-nivel-mas-bajo-en-una-decada/); [LEE Inf. 134](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/recursosdb/d/lee/inf-134-matricula-simat-lee-2026); [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/pisa-2025-results-volume-i-country-notes_2d4ff9ea-en/colombia_d64a60a2-en.html)
column7: Descriptive: demography (LEE) and composition (OECD); other causes Speculation
column8: Denominator error vs fewer over-age repeaters vs true dropout: single-age enrollment by grade against EEVV birth cohorts, GEIH attendance and rural school closures (C-600, SIMAT).

column5: Gender paradox: women lead access and graduation, lag in math and are most NEETs (Colombia, 2012-2024)
column6: Gross tertiary enrollment 45% women vs 35% men (2024); Saber 11 math gap 3.1 → 3.9 (2023-24); NEETs 1.6M women vs 816k men. [Portafolio/BanRep](https://www.portafolio.co/tendencias/sociales/estudio-revela-una-paradoja-en-la-educacion-superior-mujeres-son-mayoria-pero-persiste-una-brecha-en-esta-prueba-501336); [ICFES](https://www.icfes.gov.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2026-02_Infografia_STEAM.pdf); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/los-ninis-bajaron-5-3-al-cierre-de-2024-y-representan-22-5-del-total-de-los-jovenes-4061159)
column7: Descriptive: gap "not explained by observables" (Iregui et al., BanRep Borrador 1301, 2025)
column8: Selection into the Saber 11 test vs true performance: compare Saber 9 and Saber 11 within cohorts (Saber 5-9-11 panel), SPP/Generación E cutoffs, and GEIH care burden for female NEETs.

column5: Persistent regional test-score ranking: Boyacá, Santander, Quindío top; Chocó, Vaupés, Caribbean bottom (Colombia, to 2024)
column6: Boyacá 262 points, +5 above the mean, success concentrated in public schools; retains 83 of 100 youths; Quindío and Santander first in 2024. [Diario del Sur](https://www.diariodelsur.com.co/?p=133536); [La Silla Vacía](https://www.lasillavacia.com/?p=452167); [MEN](https://www.mineducacion.gov.co/1780/w3-article-422331.html)
column7: Descriptive: "contrast" study (Reina-Aranza & Rubio-Ramírez, BanRep DTSER 245, 2016)
column8: Smallholdings, low land inequality and normal-school density vs less conflict: border discontinuity at Boyacá's borders, IGAC land data and Saber 5/9→11 value added.

column5: PISA rises then stalls while Saber 11 falls then rises (Colombia, 2006-2025)
column6: PISA math 370 (2006) → 390 (2015) → 381 (2025); PISA coverage of 15-year-olds 60% → 75%; Saber 11 246.1 → 254.2 since 2021. [MEN](https://www.mineducacion.gov.co/1780/w3-article-417751.html); [Forbes, 8-Sep-2026](https://forbes.co/2026/09/08/actualidad/7-de-cada-10-estudiantes-en-colombia-no-alcanzan-el-nivel-minimo-en-matematicas-pruebas-pisa-2025/); [LEE Inf. 114](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/recursosdb/d/lee/inf-114-informe-saber-11-2025-lee)
column7: Descriptive (composition, pandemic); 2006-2015 rise: None
column8: Grade reweighting as over-age falls vs teaching to Saber 11 under ISCE incentives: reweight PISA by grade, use Saber 9 and an RD on Todos a Aprender (PISA, ICFES).

column5: Collapse of SENA technological-tier enrollment amid record higher education (Colombia, 2016-2023)
column6: Technological tier is the only level falling 2016-2023; −4.8% in 2023; SENA technological −8.2% in 2018-19. [ASCUN](https://ascun.org.co/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Boletin-2-Observatorio-de-Sostenibilidad-de-IES-ASCUN.pdf); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/analisis/p-harold-castilla-devoz-2912463/segun-los-numeros-como-andamos-3926736); [LEE Inf. 11](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/recursosdb/5581483/7093554/INFORME-11-LEE-PUJ-MATRICULA-SENA-2020.pdf)
column7: Descriptive: Rincón Quiñones & Espitia 2020; SENA-specific: None (MEN says it does not know why)
column8: SNIES reporting change vs crowd-out by free public tuition: program-level SNIES DiD around Ley 2307/2023, linked to SPADIES and Saber 11.

column5: Immediate transition to tertiary stuck at 38-43%; 223,000 admitted students never enroll (Colombia, 2016-2023)
column6: Immediate transition 38.0% (2016), 42.4% (2017), 43.1% (2023); 223,000 admitted per year do not enroll. [Tunja/MEN](https://mail.siedutunja.gov.co/api/planeacion/2023/1679448862034.pdf); [U. Rosario](https://urosario.edu.co/periodico-nova-et-vetera/nuestra-u/menos-de-la-mitad-de-los-bachilleres-en-colombia-logra-acceder-de-inmediato-la-educacion); [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/finanzas/223-000-cupos-en-la-educacion-superior-se-pierden-cada-ano-586187)
column7: Descriptive (financing); multiple-admission double counting not ruled out
column8: Liquidity constraints vs double-counting artefact: Saber 11-SNIES linkage with RD at scholarship thresholds (SPP, Generación E, free tuition).

column5: Persistent high urban unemployment in Ibagué, Quibdó and Cúcuta (Colombia, 2001-2025)
column6: Ibagué had "normal" unemployment until 2000; Feb 2025: Quibdó 34.9%, Ibagué 15.0%, Cúcuta 14.4%; national 8.9% in 2025, lowest since 2001. [López 2007, BanRep](https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstreams/ea649278-80b2-4126-ae7b-a07720d2a0a6/download); [DANE](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/operaciones/GEIH/cp-GEIH-feb2025.pdf); [Cambio](https://cambiocolombia.com/economia/articulo/2026/1/desempleo-en-colombia-durante-2025-fue-de-89-por-ciento-la-cifra-mas-baja-desde-2001)
column7: Descriptive (López 2007; Ayala 2014 shift-share); minimum wage Partial causal at macro level (Arango & Flórez 2016)
column8: Binding minimum wage vs persistent local demand shock: city Kaitz index × 2023-25 minimum-wage hikes vs a 2000 sectoral Bartik, using GEIH 13/23 cities, RUV and censuses.

column5: Female labor force participation stalls after ~2014, incomplete post-COVID recovery (Colombia, 2014-2024)
column6: Female gains sustained aggregate participation only until 2014; the ~40 pp gap of 1984 had halved; female LFP 56.7% (2019), 48.5% (2021), 53.4% (2024) (levels nv). [Lasso-Valderrama and Ramos-Veloza, Borrador 1326](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:bdr:borrec:1326); [GPTW](https://greatplacetowork.com.co/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2026/08/GPTW-El-Informe-Mujeres-2025.pdf)
column7: Partial causal (explains the rise, not the stall): Iregui et al. 2023, an extra child no longer reduces participation
column8: Eldercare burden vs migrant competition in feminized services: cohort pseudo-panels, migrant shift-share and older adults in household (GEIH, ECV), plus Ingreso Solidario/Renta Ciudadana rollout.

column5: Returns to post-secondary education hold at ~20% despite tripled supply (Colombia, 1995-2024)
column6: Sources conflict: returns stable since 1995 vs falling undergraduate returns vs widening wage gap 1984-2010. [Tenjo et al. 2017](https://ideas.repec.org/a/col/000438/016611.html); [Farné and Vergara 2008](https://beta.uexternado.edu.co/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/cuaderno_10.pdf); [BanRep 1984-2010](https://banrep.gov.co/es/desigualdad-salarios-colombia-evidencia-partir-encuestas-hogares-1984-2010)
column7: Partial causal: new-program penalty is student selection (Camacho, Messina & Uribe, IDB); rest Descriptive
column8: Skill-biased demand vs technical/technological composition: homogeneous GEIH 2008-2024 series with supply-expansion shift-share and OLE-PILA graduate earnings.

column5: Renting overtakes ownership; highest renter share in Latin America (Colombia, 2016-2025)
column6: ECV 2025: renting 40.8% vs owned outright 34.8%; owned outright 41.6% → 34.7% (2019-21), while renting fell 2016-18; IDB: 39.1% vs 21.2% regional. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/este-es-el-porcentaje-de-colombianos-con-vivienda-propia-estadisticas-y-datos-actualizados-581776); [DANE](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/investigaciones/condiciones_vida/calidad_vida/2021/comunicado_ECV_2021.pdf); [Última Hora](https://www.ultimahora.com/el-812-los-departamentos-se-destinan-al-alquiler-segun-el-bid-n1132792)
column7: Descriptive (BanRep on rents; Clavijo, Janna & Muñoz 2005); interest rates: Speculation
column8: Household fragmentation and Venezuelan migration vs subsidies capitalized into prices: shift-share decomposition (head age, size, nationality), ownership-at-35 cohorts and Fonvivienda allocations (ECV, GEIH).

column5: Persistently low household saving (Colombia, to 2023)
column6: Household saving 7.2% of disposable income; gross saving 10.1% of GDP in 2023, lowest since 1960; −1.6% among lower-middle-income urban households. [BanRep REF](https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstreams/3f9ac784-cb15-4a6f-add4-b71666aa85eb/download); [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/economia/2024/04/02/esto-dijo-juan-daniel-oviedo-ex-director-del-dane-sobre-las-cifras-del-ahorro-bruto-del-pais-1083163/); [BanRep be_960](https://d1b4gd4m8561gs.cloudfront.net/sites/default/files/publicaciones/archivos/be_960.pdf)
column7: Descriptive (classic BanRep literature)
column8: Saving held in motorcycles and self-built housing rather than financial assets: durable-goods spending in ECV and BanRep's household financial burden survey, with rigorous regional comparison.

column5: Motorcycle boom (62% of fleet) and U-shaped road mortality (Colombia, 1998-2025)
column6: RUNT 2024: 62% of ~20M vehicles, 816,513 new motorcycles; 6.16M households own one, 95.1% in strata 1-3; road deaths per 100k 21.6 → 12.7 → 16.7, 63% motorcyclists, Casanare 37.8. [RUNT](https://runt.gov.co/sites/default/files/documentos/Balance%20del%20Sector%20Tr%C3%A1nsito%20y%20Transporte%202024.pdf); [Infobae, 22-May-2026](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/05/22/colombia-sobre-dos-ruedas-61-millones-de-hogares-ya-tienen-moto-y-el-fenomeno-no-se-detiene/); [Vanguardia, 28-Oct-2026](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2026/10/28/muertes-en-moto-en-colombia-aumentan-y-ya-representan-el-63-de-las-victimas-viales/)
column7: Partial (fleet-size exposure); Descriptive: Sincelejo moto-taxis (Sánchez-Jabba, BanRep)
column8: Motorcycle as self-employment capital vs transit substitute: staggered BRT/SETP entry, delivery-platform arrival and credit shift-share on municipal RUNT, GEIH and EEVV (V20-V29).

column5: Coffee Axis "syndrome": ageing, emigration, remittances, ultra-low fertility, high suicide, high life satisfaction (Colombia, 1990-2024)

column6: Catholics 91-95% (1950-70) → 79% (2014); 67% Catholic and 16% non-Catholic Christian (Beltrán); ~20% no religion in 2024. column8: Pentecostalism as a commitment technology for alcohol, saving, domestic violence and schooling: registered church openings by municipality-year (Ley 133/1994) with ENDR 2019 and LAPOP.

column5: Gestational syphilis quadruples while congenital syphilis stays at 5× the elimination target (Colombia, 2014-2025)

column5: Maternal mortality 6-7× national in Chocó and Vichada; Afro-Colombian women now highest (Colombia, 2015-2024)
column6: National early MMR 44.3 (2024); Chocó 308.5, Vichada 273.2 (to verify; DANE gives Chocó 121.5); highest MMR in the OECD. column8: Referral-network failure vs public-hospital quality under EPS non-payment vs armed blockades: travel time to cesarean-capable care (REPS), EPS liquidation shocks, CERAC/ACLED, severe maternal morbidity as larger-n outcome (SIVIGILA 549/551).

column5: Institutional delivery falls in La Guajira and Guainía while Vaupés converges (Colombia, 2015-2024)
column6: La Guajira 98.4% → 96.3%; Guainía 91.6% → 89.6%; Vaupés +14.2 pp to 69.9% (search-only). [DANE EEVV 2024pr](https://www.dane.gov.co/files/operaciones/EEVV/2025/26-mar-2025/bol-EEVV-2024pr.pdf)

column8: Venezuelan and Wayuu migrant mothers vs better registration of home births: nationality × place of birth by municipality-year (Uribia, Manaure, Maicao) and registration delay in EEVV and REPS.

column5: Exclusive breastfeeding falls while early initiation rises (Colombia, 2005-2015)
column6: Exclusive breastfeeding 46.9% (2005) → 42.8% (2010) → 36.1% (2015); early initiation up to 72%; mean exclusive duration 1.8 months. [MinSalud ENSIN 2015](https://www.minsalud.gov.co/Paginas/Gobierno-presenta-Encuesta-Nacional-de-Situaci%C3%B3n-Nutricional-de-Colombia-ENSIN-2015.aspx); [Consultorsalud](https://consultorsalud.com/lactancia-materna-en-colombia-un-desafio/)

column8: Cesarean rise delaying lactogenesis vs female work and informality: delivery mode × breastfeeding within mother, and leave reforms (Ley 1468/2011, Ley 1822/2017) × formal employment, using ENSIN 2005-2015 and ENDS.

column5: Suicide among children aged 10-14 and Indigenous youth in Vaupés and the Amazon (Colombia, 2013-2024)
column6: 1.73 per 100k at ages 10-14 (2015); 63 cases (2013) → 107 (2017); 90 cases Jan-Oct 2024; Vaupés Indigenous youth rate "almost ten times" the national rate. column8: Real programme effects vs cause reclassification vs shrinking child cohort: EEVV deaths vs SIVIGILA 113, rates vs counts, and municipal programme rollout.

column5: Más Familias en Acción benefit amounts by municipal group (Colombia, Law 1532 of Jun-2012; 2013+)
column6: Group 3 split from group 4 at a 70% municipal MPI (Census 2005); health incentive COP 60,000 (groups 1-3) vs 70,000 (group 4) (nv). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/2013/01/09/mas-familias-en-accion-contara-con-presupuesto-de-17-billones/); [Seminario CEDE](https://economia.uniandes.edu.co/sites/default/files/seminariocede/RedisenoFeA-Uniandes.pdf)
column7: Not studied (provisional); Villa (2018) RD covers only the original design
column8: Does a larger incentive (group 4 vs 3) change school attendance, growth check-ups and malnutrition? Municipal RD at the predetermined 2005 MPI = 70% cutoff with SIMAT, Vital Statistics, Saber 11; first stage may be small.

column5: Transition from Familias en Acción to Renta Ciudadana (Colombia, Apr-2023; new design Jan-2024)
column6: First RC payment 29-Apr-2023; FA "closing cycle" and suspensions for SISBEN inconsistencies; per-household design with weakened conditionality from 1-Jan-2024; 3,651,920 households in 2024-2025. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/economia/2023/04/20/transito-a-renta-ciudadana-primer-pago-del-subsidio-comenzara-el-29-de-abril-994689/); [La Silla Vacía](https://www.lasillavacia.com/?p=360985)
column7: Not studied; only a UNAD master's thesis on management (2025)
column8: Did moving from a per-child CCT to a per-household transfer with weaker conditionality reduce school attendance and growth check-ups? Event study on transition date × prior intensity (eligible children, municipal group); DPS payment data via petition, SIMAT.

column5: Renta Ciudadana "Valoración del Cuidado" line (Colombia, Apr-May 2024 onward)
column6: First cycle paid COP 500,000 to 519,408 households (544,108 on Mar-2024 list); requires SISBEN IV Group A and children under 6; single-parent headship as requirement unconfirmed (nv). [Radio Nacional](https://radionacional.co/actualidad/economia/renta-ciudadana-2024-como-cobrar-primer-pago); [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/lista-de-beneficiarios-de-renta-ciudadana-marzo-2024-veala-aqui/)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Does an unconditional transfer to single mothers of young children change female labor supply, CDI use and child health? Exit when youngest child turns 6 (birth-date design) plus RD at Group A/B border; GEIH, SISBEN IV (restricted).

column5: Renta Ciudadana payment shocks (Colombia, 2025)
column6: Banco Agrario announced as operator 29-Apr-2025; May-2025 disruptions; 4th cycle postponed to 25-Sep to 13-Oct-2025 for RUI review; DPS said almost one in two households could exit; end of "Colombia sin Hambre" (conflicting). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/2025/04/29/subsidios-del-gobierno-tienen-nuevo-operador-quien-asumira-el-pago/); [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/renta-ciudadana-y-devolucion-del-iva-cuando-pagan-en-septiembre-y-quienes-podrian-dejar-de-recibir-el-subsidio/)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Do payment delays, uncertainty and mass exits affect food consumption, school attendance and gota-a-gota borrowing? High-frequency event study on the shifted cycle; DiD on municipal density of Banco Agrario vs SuRed points; GEIH, Pulso Social.

column5: SISBEN III to IV and shift from Jóvenes en Acción to Renta Joven (Colombia, 2022-2026)
column6: Res. 00851/2022 transition regime for SISBEN III entrants; last JeA cycle Dec-2023; Renta Joven up to COP 400,000; 2nd payment from 9-Jul-2025 (>201,000 youth); 2025 "cycle 6" paid 18-Feb-2026 (numbering inconsistent). [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2025/07/09/prosperidad-social-inicia-segundo-pago-de-renta-joven-mas-de-201000-beneficiarios/); [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/cargues/avance/compilacion/docs/resolucion_daps_0851_2022.htm)
column7: Little studied; UIS thesis on JeA and dropout 2012-2019; nothing on Renta Joven
column8: Does losing or delayed enrollment-conditioned transfers raise higher-education and SENA dropout? Compare cohorts protected by SISBEN III vs SISBEN IV entrants, SISBEN IV cutoff, cycle-6 delay; SPADIES (restricted), SNIES, Saber Pro.

column5: VAT refund (Devolución del IVA) 2023 changes and extraordinary payment (Colombia, 2023-2024)
column6: Amount COP 80,000 to 89,000 per cycle (conflicting, nv); ~2 million households (~700,000 new) selected by vulnerability ranking with budget cutoff; extraordinary payment (>COP 135,000M) for uncollected cycles 4-6 of 2023. [Valora Analitik](https://www.valoraanalitik.com/?p=387806); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/inicia-pago-extraordinario-de-la-devolucion-del-iva-para-los-ciclos-4-5-y-6-de-2023-3883790)
column7: Little studied (provisional); only distributive simulations (UNLP DT 42); a 2020 pilot evaluation may exist
column8: What explains non-collection of a small transfer: distance to payment point or amount? RD on the priority-score cutoff; staggered entry of 700,000 new households; re-offer via extraordinary payment; DPS collection records via petition.

column5: Comptroller (CGR) targeting alerts on transfer programs (Colombia, May-2022; Aug-2024)
column6: 3,087,207 transfers (>COP 402,000M) to 390,131 beneficiaries with eligibility problems in 2021; 19,951 deceased (COP 3,843M); Aug-2024 statement: payments to deceased continue. [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/noticias/2022/05/09/contraloria-detecto-mas-de-402-mil-millones-en-giros-a-colados-y-fallecidos-en-el-sisben/); [CGR Comunicado 152-24](https://www.ambitojuridico.com/sites/default/files/2024-08/COMUNICADO-152-24.pdf)
column7: Not studied; older SISBEN accuracy work (Castañeda 2005)
column8: Did audit alerts trigger purges that cut improper payments but also excluded legitimate beneficiaries? Municipal intensity of findings × report date (no clean threshold); CGR reports, DANE deaths, SISBEN IV, election results.

column5: Colombia Mayor benefit raised by age and sex (Colombia, May-2024 and Oct-2025)
column6: Res. 00809/2024: age 80+ from COP 80,000 to 225,000; Res. 02229 of 24-Sep-2025: women 70+ and men 75+ to COP 230,000 from ~30-Oct-2025; signed resolutions not seen (nv); 2026 amounts conflict. [Prosperidad Social](https://prosperidadsocial.gov.co/Noticias/colombia-mayor-prosperidad-social-aumenta-el-monto-de-la-transferencia-para-mayores-de-80-anos/); [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/economia/gobierno-aumento-subsidio-de-colombia-mayor-desde-el-30-de-octubre-953491)
column7: Not studied (top-5 case); all work predates 2024 (Pfutze and Rodríguez-Castelán 2015/2019)
column8: Does tripling the social pension change consumption, health, mortality, living arrangements and household labor supply? Age RD at 80 and sex-specific 70/75 cutoffs, difference-in-discontinuities around each resolution; public DANE deaths by single age and municipality.

column5: Colombia Mayor municipal quotas and waiting lists (Colombia, 2025)
column6: Fixed municipal quotas filled by age and SISBEN score; Popayán Dec-2025 expansion to 19,500 (~11,000 from waiting list), payments from 23-Dec-2025; Armenia 129 and 65 new slots. [El País Cali](https://www.elpais.com.co/colombia/en-popayan-se-amplia-la-cobertura-de-colombia-mayor-a-19500-beneficiarios-esto-es-lo-que-se-sabe-1809.html); [Alcaldía de Armenia](https://armenia.gov.co/buenas-noticias-129-cupos-nuevos-para-colombia-mayor-en-armenia)
column7: Not studied / possibly Little studied; DNP/Econometría Sinergia evaluation may use rationing (to check)
column8: Does receiving the pension sooner, with less time on the waiting list, improve health, mortality and household welfare? RD on priority score within municipality-cycle; staggered expansions (Callaway-Sant'Anna); DPS lists via petition, DANE deaths.

column5: Payment operator change for Colombia Mayor and Renta Ciudadana (Colombia, Jul-2026)
column6: Around 14-Jul-2026 Banco Agrario exits; a SuRed-SuperGiros joint venture takes over with >31,000 points and a "Payments Manager" for bank accounts. [El Oriente](https://www.eloriente.com/articulo/banco-agrario-se-despide-los-beneficiarios-de-renta-ciudadana-y-colombia-mayor-deberaacuten-cambiar-su-lugar-de-cobro-a-uacuteltimo-momento/55642); [El Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/colombia/actualidad-co/oficial-prosperidad-social-saca-al-banco-agrario-y-confirma-nuevos-operadores-para-los-principales-subsidios)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Did moving from bank branches to agents and remittance networks change collection rates, costs and financial inclusion of rural elderly? DiD: municipalities where Banco Agrario was the only point vs those with SuperGiros/SuRed; DPS uncollected payments, Banca de las Oportunidades coverage.

column5: SISBEN IV 2026 update and municipal purges (Colombia, Oct-2025 to 2026)
column6: From Jan-2026 administrative records prevail over self-report; 29.78% of >1.6 million households changed group (fact per El Tiempo, "could" per Portafolio; nv); Barranquilla Res. 001 of 14-Oct-2025 on 14,891 records. [El Tiempo](https://www.eltiempo.com/economia/finanzas-personales/actualizacion-del-sisben-iv-cambio-la-clasificacion-de-casi-el-30-de-los-hogares-asi-puede-consultarla-3542286); [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/mis-finanzas/vivienda/la-actualizacion-del-sisben-en-2026-podria-cambiar-la-clasificacion-de-casi-3-de-cada-10-hogares-en-colombia-492099)
column7: Not studied; only an unrelated RD using 2015 SISBEN (Medellín participatory budget)
column8: What happens to subsidized-health enrollment, program retention and formal employment of upward-reclassified households, and are there strategic responses? Staggered rollout and mechanical reclassification; SISBEN IV microdata via DNP agreement, BDUA.

column5: Universal Income Registry (RUI) replacing SISBEN (Colombia, Aug-2026 onward)
column6: Created by art. 70 of Law 2294/2023; targeting tool from 1-Aug-2026 (Decree 662/2026, text nv), transition to 31-Oct-2026; Sep-2026 failures (senior officials classified as poor); extension draft to Jul- or Dec-2027 (nv). [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/gobierno-aplazo-para-el-1-de-agosto-la-transicion-del-sisben-al-registro-universal-de-ingresos-4432632); [Cambio](https://cambiocolombia.com/poder/articulo/2026/9/gobierno-abelardo-espriella-sisben-fallas-subsidios)
column7: Not studied; only a 2019 article on SISBEN and stratification targeting
column8: How do inclusion and exclusion errors change from a proxy-means test to an administrative income registry, and what happens to switchers? Double RD at both instruments' cutoffs; DNP data (not public); document chronology now, use 2027 data.

column5: Solidarity basic income under pension reform, Law 2381/2024 (Colombia, effective 1-Apr-2027)
column6: Converts Colombia Mayor into ~COP 230,000 income run by DPS (reference COP 223,800 for 2025); 1-Jul-2025 start suspended; ruling C-264/2026 (reported 25-Aug-2026) sets 1-Apr-2027; Colpensiones asked for 2028. [El Tiempo](https://www.eltiempo.com/economia/finanzas-personales/guia-practica-con-preguntas-y-respuestas-para-entender-que-ha-pasado-con-la-reforma-pensional-y-cuando-estara-lista-3471567); [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/gobierno/corte-constitucional-publica-fallo-sobre-la-reforma-pensional-que-quedo-en-firme-y-que-vuelve-al-congreso-502563)
column7: Not studied / Little studied (descriptive only; IDEAS paper on the non-contributory pillar, author nv)
column8: If the solidarity income changes ages, scores or coverage, what are the effects of the new cutoff? A future, dated cutoff (1-Apr-2027) allows a pre-registered design using the same data as SP-A8.

column5: ICBF early-childhood service gaps from late contracting (Colombia, 2023-2024)
column6: National tender closed 23-Jan-2024; 786 community-based organizations prioritized; Santander >8,000 children without care in Feb-2024; Comptroller: ">780,000 children a month without care" (year nv). [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/area-metropolitana/bucaramanga/protesta-de-madres-comunitarias-llego-febrero-y-aun-no-hay-contratos-para-atender-a-8000-ninos-en-santander-YC8532346); [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/node/256334); [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/educacion/mas-de-780-mil-ninos-menores-de-5-anos-llevan-un-mes-sin-atencion-del-icbf-contraloria/)
column7: Not studied (top-5 case); Bernal et al. (2019) evaluates service type, another margin
column8: Do weeks or months without care affect child nutrition, maternal employment and school readiness? Gap duration per contract (SECOP II start date vs 1-Jan) × switch to community operators; weekly municipal SIVIGILA 113 (public), GEIH.

column5: Unfinished or idle CDIs ("white elephants") (Colombia, 2015-2025)
column6: Bolívar: 2015 project for 22 CDIs, CGR seeks to rescue 9; Barrancabermeja CDI delivered 2019, ~3 years idle, now serves 188 children; Soledad: COP 1,042M to recover a CDI (29-Apr-2025). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/regional/2025/04/01/recuperacion-de-cdi-en-bolivar-el-proyecto-que-cambiara-el-futuro-infantil/); [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/atlantico/2025/04/29/contraloria-proyecta-inversion-de-1042-millones-para-recuperar-cdi-nueva-esperanza-en-soledad/)
column7: Not studied on delays; Bernal et al. (2019) covers another margin
column8: Does late or failed CDI opening change institutional coverage, maternal labor supply and local nutrition? Event study across municipalities with on-time, delayed or never-opened CDIs; CGR and FDN/Findeter lists via petition, SECOP, SIVIGILA 113.

column5: Community mothers: minimum-wage stipend (Feb-2014) and formalization (Colombia, 2014; 2023-2025)
column6: Law 1607/2012 art. 36: stipend equal to minimum wage from 1-Feb-2014; Decree 289/2014 labor contracts; Feb-2023 agreement with 18-month formalization; Law 2466/2025 for ~60,000 mothers. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2023/02/11/el-icbf-llego-a-un-acuerdo-con-sindicato-para-levantar-paro-de-madres-comunitarias/); [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/node/299050)
column7: Little studied; legal and qualitative only
column8: Does raising caregivers' pay to the minimum wage change their retention and selection, care quality and child outcomes? Intensity of the stipend-minimum wage gap and local minimum-wage bite, plus regional formalization cohorts; GEIH, PILA (restricted), SIVIGILA 113.

column5: Nutritional Recovery Centers (CRN) in La Guajira after ruling T-302/2017 (Colombia, 2022-2024)
column6: CRN expansion since 2022; ICBF reports 13 CRN 24/7 and 6,472 children served; 95 of 265 deceased children were in ICBF programs; INS: -45% malnutrition deaths in 2024 (ICBF: -40%). [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/node/368863); [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/95-ninos-que-murieron-por-desnutricion-en-la-guajira-estaban-en-programas-del-icbf-CA9453657); [Consultorsalud](https://consultorsalud.com/?p=290903)
column7: Not studied in economics; only a UNAD intervention proposal
column8: Does opening a nearby CRN reduce mortality and severity of acute malnutrition among Wayuu children? Staggered openings × distance from rancherías, Cesar/Magdalena controls; SIVIGILA 113, Vital Statistics; risks: reporting bias, few clusters.

column5: Bienestarina supply interruption and new contract (Colombia, May-2021; Dec-2022)
column6: National Strike blockades halted production and transport (64 tonnes held in Cartago); 2021 tender for 18,300 t/year; contract to 2027 for ~COP 1.1 trillion (29-Dec-2022). [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/colombia/2021/05/26/contraloria-pide-desbloquear-vias-para-permitir-transporte-de-bienestarina-820440/); [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2022/12/29/hay-contrato-de-produccion-de-bienestarina-en-colombia-hasta-2027/)
column7: Little studied; ICBF Bienestarina evaluation Phase II assesses the product as a program
column8: Did the May-2021 interruption worsen nutrition of ICBF-dependent children by exposure to blocked routes? Blockades × distance to plants × prior delivery intensity; confounded by COVID and the strike; ICBF deliveries via petition, SIVIGILA 113.

column5: Child-protection (PARD) reform, Law 1878 (Colombia, Jan-2018)
column6: Single six-month term (previously four; "18 months" premise was wrong); non-observance of rights no longer grounds for opening; ~127,000 children under protection (nv); 5,159 children without adoptability decision (date nv). [ICBF Concepto 11B](https://www.icbf.gov.co/sites/default/files/normas/CONCEPTO%2011B%20DE%202018.docx); [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/icbf-tiene-a-5159-ninos-sin-definirles-si-seran-o-no-adoptados-HD5702786)
column7: Not studied in economics; legal work only
column8: Did shorter deadlines change time in out-of-home care, family reunification and time to adoption? Cohorts entering PARD before vs after Jan-2018 (survival analysis or RD on entry date); ICBF SIM data via agreement or petition.

column5: Late PAE start by territorial entity (ETC) and year (Colombia, 2022-2026)
column6: 2022: 65 of 92 ETCs started on time (67 per another source); Jul-2022: ~183,731 students without PAE; Jan-2026: >860,000 students at risk from delays in 17 ETCs. [Radio Nacional](https://www.radionacional.co/actualidad/pae-65-entidades-territoriales-iniciaron-tiempo); [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2026/01/18/mas-de-860000-estudiantes-podrian-iniciar-2026-sin-alimentacion-escolar-por-retrasos-en-el-pae/)
column7: Not studied on delays (top-5 case); CEDE 2024-24 and 2026-40 study expansion (check 2026-40 start dates)
column8: Do PAE-less days at the start of the year reduce attendance and effective enrollment and raise within-year dropout? DiD on days of delay (SECOP II contract start vs ETC calendar), 2024 new-mayor shock; SIMAT, Saber 3-5-9 and 11.

column5: Over 100 days without PAE in Magdalena (Colombia, 2022)
column6: OCAD approved PAE 6-Dec-2021 with ICBF as executor (legally challenged); >147,000 students without service >100 days (Jul-2022); four award postponements in 2023; analogous Cauca Aug-2023 (>30,000 students). [Radio Nacional](https://www.radionacional.co/regiones/caribe/pae-en-magdalena-140-mil-estudiantes-afectados-por-retrasos); [Semana](https://www.semana.com/nacion/barranquilla/articulo/cero-y-van-cuatro-los-aplazamientos-para-contratar-al-operador-del-pae-en-magdalena-que-esta-pasando/202340/)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Does a >100-day suspension raise dropout and lower Saber 11 and Saber 3-5-9? DiD or synthetic control: non-certified Magdalena municipalities vs Santa Marta and the Caribbean; SIMAT, Saber 11 2022; post-pandemic confound, Ciénaga status to verify.

column5: PAE during school vacations: PAE+ (2023), baskets (2024), PAE en Receso (2026) (Colombia, 2023-2026)
column6: Launched Jun-2023 in La Guajira: baskets for ~600,000 students in 109 municipalities of 17 departments; 577,000 baskets in 2024; Cali not prioritized; 1.4 million baskets in 2026 (722,000 in June, election year). [Cambio](https://cambiocolombia.com/pais/articulo/2023/6/en-que-consiste-el-programa-pae-que-presento-el-gobierno-en-la-guajira); [Alcaldía de Cali](https://www.cali.gov.co/boletines/publicaciones/192984/ministerio-de-educacion-no-priorizo-a-cali-para-la-entrega-de-canastas-alimentarias-del-pae-durante-el-receso-escolar/); [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/06/18/la-uapa-rechazo-fines-electorales-en-la-entrega-de-722000-canastas-del-pae-en-municipios-con-alta-inseguridad-alimentaria/)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Do vacation baskets reduce post-break drops in attendance and enrollment, or malnutrition, in prioritized municipalities? RD if MEN used an index threshold (act not found), else matched DiD; coverage changes 2023-2026; UApA list via petition, SIMAT Jan vs Nov.

column5: "PAE at home" during COVID-19 (Colombia, Mar-2020 to 2021)
column6: Decree 470 and UApA Res. 006 of 25-Mar-2020: ready-to-eat ration, take-home ration or voucher; all 96 ETCs (~5.6 million students); at one cut 87% take-home, 6% ready-to-eat; return to on-site PAE on varying 2021 dates. [UApA Res. 0006](https://escuelasecretarias.mineducacion.gov.co/sites/default/files/2022-10/Resoluci%C3%B3n%20No.%200006%20del%2025%20de%20marzo%20de%202020%20de%20la%20Unidad%20Administrativa%20Especial%20de%20Alimentaci%C3%B3n%20Escolar.pdf); [UApA weekly report](https://escuelasecretarias.mineducacion.gov.co/sites/default/files/2022-10/Informe%20de%20operaci%C3%B3n%20Programa%20de%20Alimentaci%C3%B3n%20Escolar%2014052021.pdf)
column7: Little studied; descriptive CEDID Ciudad Bolívar case study, CEPAL fact sheet
column8: Did ETCs that delivered monthly take-home rations or resumed earlier see less 2020-2021 dropout? ETC × week panel of modality, first-delivery and return dates from public UApA reports; SIMAT, Saber 11; modality choice is endogenous.

column5: Mandatory local food procurement in PAE (Colombia, 2015-2025)
column6: MEN Res. 16432/2015 set at least 20% from smallholders; Law 2046 of 6-Aug-2020 raised it to at least 30% (Decree 248/2021); Directive 9 of 2024; MEN strategy Jul-2025. [Colombia Compra](https://colombiacompra.gov.co/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/boletin_de_relatoria_-_edicion_vi.pdf); [INVIMA](https://normograma.invima.gov.co/normograma/docs/pdf/ley_2046_2020.pdf)
column7: Little studied; critical essay (Acevedo), UniMinuto thesis 2025; none causal
column8: Did the local-purchase floor raise smallholder incomes, or make PAE contracting costlier and slower? Prior intensity (PAE share of local demand; CNA 2014 smallholder supply) × rule date; local bidders before and after in SECOP II; EVA.

column5: PAE technical guidelines change (Colombia, Dec-2017 to 2021)
column6: Res. 29452 of 29-Dec-2017; Res. 1750/2018 created a transition regime for ETCs with projects filed before a Feb-2018 cutoff; replaced by Res. 335/2021. [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/cargues/avance/compilacion/docs/resolucion_mineducacion_29452_2017.htm); [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/cargues/avance/compilacion/docs/resolucion_mineducacion_1750_2018.htm)
column7: Not studied; none found
column8: Did stricter standards change cost per ration, number of bidders or service interruptions? ETCs inside vs outside the 2018 transition regime by project filing date; SECOP I and II bidder and price data.

column5: Gota a gota (informal moneylending) and the CREO credit line (Colombia, 2019-2025)
column6: Per EMICRON, gota a gota rose from 13.9% (2019) to 24.4% of microbusiness credit sources; CREO formalized by Decree 2120 of 11-Dec-2023 (15,779 beneficiaries by 31-Jan-2024); Decree 1396 of 22-Dec-2025 raised the cap (nv). [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/negocios/empresas/gota-a-gota-es-casi-el-25-del-credito-entre-microempresas-565190); [RTVC](https://www.rtvcnoticias.com/linea-de-credito-creo-como-acceder-este-programa-que-busca-acabar-con-el-gota-gota); [MinCIT](https://www.mincit.gov.co/prensa/noticias/documentos-noticias/decreto-1396-del-22-de-diciembre-de-2025.aspx)
column7: Little studied; correlational logit (Hernández García and Oviedo Gómez 2016), ethnographies
column8: Does subsidized small formal credit reduce gota-a-gota use and arrears, or only reach the already bankable? Bunching at old and new caps (Decree 1396), intermediary expansion, EMICRON pseudo-panel; CREO records via petition; low power.

column5: VAT on online betting switched on and off (Colombia, Feb-2025 to Apr-2026)
column6: Decree-Law 175 of 14-Feb-2025: 19% VAT on deposits from 22-Feb-2025 to 31-Dec-2025; Decree 1474 (Dec-2025) reimposed it; Court suspended it 28-Jan-2026, struck down Apr-2026; Fecoljuegos claims deposits -30% to -50%, Coljuegos figures rose. [Forbes](https://forbes.co/economia-y-finanzas/gobierno-expidio-decreto-que-impone-iva-del-19-a-los-juegos-de-suerte-y-azar-en-linea-con-el-que-busca-500-000-millones); [Semana](https://www.semana.com/economia/macroeconomia/articulo/corte-tumba-iva-del-19-a-licores-y-apuestas-en-linea-tambien-hay-cambios-en-el-impuesto-al-patrimonio/202628/); [Sigma](https://sigma.world/es/news/diferencias-datos-juego-en-linea-colombia/)
column7: Not studied; EAN qualitative thesis, Lancet Regional Health-Americas commentary
column8: Does a sharp rise in betting costs cut gambling spending and improve youth arrears and nanocredit use, or shift betting to illegal sites? Event study/RD in time on on-off dates; Coljuegos monthly aggregates, DIAN, bureau or bank data.

column5: Law 2157 "Borrón y cuenta nueva" credit-record amnesty (Colombia, Nov-2021 to Oct-2022)
column6: In force Nov-2021 with 12-month transition; negative data erased at most 6 months after payment, expires at 8 years; 1.7 million beneficiaries vs 16 million projected; "2.0" bill (PL 024/2025) filed 20-Jul-2025, not enacted. [INCP](https://incp.org.co/publicaciones/infoincp-publicaciones/informacion-para-empresas/entorno/financiero/2021/11/ley-de-borron-y-cuenta-nueva-comienza-a-regir-oficialmente-en-colombia/); [Enter.co](https://www.enter.co/colombia/borron-y-cuenta-nueva-2-0-el-proyecto-de-ley-que-promete-borrar-reportes-en-datacredito-y-otras-centrales-de-riesgo/)
column7: Little studied; legal analysis only; Bos, Morales and Roszbach on Law 1266/2008 (firms); Chilean comparator (Liberman et al.)
column8: Does erasing negative credit history expand formal credit and reduce informal borrowing, or do lenders tighten for everyone? Eligibility by payment date within the window, individual DiD, municipal shift-share; needs credit-bureau agreement.

column5: Low-amount consumer credit ("nanocredits") (Colombia, Dec-2014 to 2026)
column6: Decree 2654 of 17-Dec-2014: loans up to 2 minimum wages, 36 months; reformed by Decree 222/2020; monthly usury cap from Jan-2026; Jul-2026 cap 62.66% EA vs 28.79% for ordinary consumer credit. [ICEF](https://www.icef.com.co/component/k2/item/983-gobierno-crea-nuevo-tipo-de-credito-dirigido-a-poblacion-de-bajos-ingresos); [Valora Analitik](https://www.valoraanalitik.com/?p=593524)
column7: Little studied; descriptive Banca de las Oportunidades study 2018-2021 (2007 microcredit usury cap already studied)
column8: Does a formal product with its own usury cap substitute for gota a gota or create over-indebtedness? 2015 entry, 2020 eligibility change, monthly usury gap since 2026, lender entry dates; Superfinanciera rates, EMICRON, bureau.

column5: Bre-B interoperable instant payments (Colombia, Jul-Oct 2025)
column6: Key registration from 14-Jul-2025; full operation 6-Oct-2025; >82 million keys at launch, ~95 million by Dec-2025; 218 entities in Jan-2026. [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/cuenta-regresiva-para-el-inicio-de-bre-b-usuarios-deben-empezar-a-registrar-sus-llaves/); [Actualícese](https://actualicese.com/bre-b-ya-esta-operando-oficialmente-y-van-mas-de-82-millones-de-llaves-registradas/)
column7: Not studied causally; descriptive BanRep working paper (2026)
column8: Do free instant payments reduce cash use and the cost of receiving transfers and domestic remittances? Weak variation: simultaneous national launch, only prior exposure to wallets or QR merchants; BanRep aggregates, Financial Capabilities survey.

column5: REDAM child-support debtors registry, Law 2097 (Colombia, Jul-2021; regulated 2022)
column6: Law of 2-Jul-2021, regulated by Decree 1310/2022; threshold of three missed payments; registration decided by a judge, not automatic; sanctions include travel ban and asset-sale limits; ">140,000" debtors figure unreliable (nv). [Brigard Urrutia](https://www.bu.com.co/es/insights/noticias/decreto-1310-de-2022-por-el-cual-se-reglamenta-el-redam); [Agencia Nacional de Defensa Jurídica](https://and.gov.co/noticias/redam-en-que-consiste-este-registro)
column7: Not studied; legal thesis, Dejusticia; related Guarín and Ham González (IZA DP 18506, 2026)
