column8: Do non-monetary sanctions on debtor fathers raise support payments, separated mothers' labor supply and child schooling, or induce informality or emigration? 2022 rollout × prior municipal non-support complaints; fuzzy 3-payment threshold; GEIH, ELCA, Fiscalía.

column5: Unilateral divorce, Law 2442 (Colombia, 27-Dec-2024)
column6: Allows divorce by one spouse's will (Civil Code art. 154); notarial divorces 24,277 (2019), 16,554 (2020), 25,272 in 2023 (28,239 per another source); unilateral cases go to courts, absent from notarial series. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/gobierno/divorcio-libre-de-que-se-trata-la-ley-sancionada-por-gustavo-petro-620914); [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2025/12/31/segun-supernotariado-en-2025-los-colombianos-se-casaron-y-se-divorciaron-menos-las-personas-estan-pensando-mas-en-las-mascotas/)
column7: Not studied in economics; law and social-work articles only
column8: Did unilateral divorce change married women's labor supply, child investment or domestic violence (as in Stevenson and Wolfers)? Single-date reform: married vs cohabiting couples, court congestion by circuit; GEIH, SIVIGILA 875, Medicina Legal.

column5: Shelters (casas refugio) for women victims of violence (Colombia, 2019-2026)
column6: Decree 1630/2019, Law 2215/2022 (progressive rollout), Decree 75/2024; in 2021 only 8 shelters for 1,103 municipalities; Bogotá 6 shelters, budget up to COP 12,597M in 2024; a judge ordered a governorship to open shelters. [Senado](https://senado.gov.co/index.php/el-senado/noticias/3010-proyecto-de-ley-busca-aumentar-el-numero-de-casas-refugio-para-mujeres-en-riesgo-por-violencia); [Radio Nacional](https://radionacional.co/noticias-colombia/red-nacional-de-casas-refugio-la-estrategia-del-ministerio-de-igualdad-y-equidad); [Rama Judicial](https://portalhistorico.ramajudicial.gov.co/documents/2307298/97220355/CSJCAC22-86.pdf/13f0970b-e86b-4213-ae6a-595346e6e467)
column7: Not studied; psychology thesis (2020), Berkeley HRC report (2013)
column8: Does opening a shelter increase reporting of partner violence and reduce femicides? Staggered openings 2019-2026 (Callaway-Sant'Anna), court-ordered openings as instrument; SIVIGILA 875, Medicina Legal; confidential dates via petition (municipal level suffices).

column5: Online recruitment of minors by armed groups (Colombia, 2021-2026)
column6: Police (5-Jul-2024): 101 social-media recruitment cases in 2024, 47 in Cauca, 63 TikTok accounts; HRW: ~1,500 minors recruited since 2021; ~44% of 2025 recruits contacted via social media; figures inconsistent, underreported. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2024/07/05/grupos-armados-estarian-reclutando-menores-por-redes-sociales-este-ano-se-han-registrado-101-casos/); [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/08/24/i-thought-id-never-see-my-mom-again/recruitment-and-use-of-children-by-colombian); [MercoPress](https://en.mercopress.com/2026/08/24/almost-half-the-minors-recruited-by-armed-groups-in-2025-were-approached-via-social-media)
column7: Little studied; qualitative work (Bjørkhaug MICROCON WP 27; Hurtado et al. 2018)
column8: Did 4G or TikTok arrival in municipalities with armed presence raise recruitment and school dropout? 4G antenna rollout (MinTIC/CRC) × prior armed presence, post-2016 dissident expansion; ICBF demobilized-children data, Defensoría alerts, SIMAT.

column5: Webcam modeling industry (Colombia, 2020s; low promise)
column6: 100,000-300,000 models (Forbes); US$600 million revenue (La República); Cali, Medellín and Bogotá ~70%; Sep-2023 regulation bill rejected by models; no approved dated trigger, flagged low promise. [Forbes](https://forbes.co/actualidad/un-vacio-legal-y-pocas-oportunidades-el-limbo-que-hace-a-colombia-una-meca-de-webcamers); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/ocio/industria-webcam-ya-factura-us-600-millones-y-cuenta-con-al-menos-100-000-modelos-3554180)
column7: Not studied; other-discipline works (titles nv)
column8: Did this dollar-denominated external demand change young women's labor participation, schooling or fertility? Exchange-rate shifts, studio openings in business registries (RUES), migrant inflows; GEIH cannot identify the activity.

column5: Emberá youth suicide in Risaralda, Mistrató and Pueblo Rico (Colombia, recent years, dates unspecified; low promise)
column6: Complaints by the CRIR indigenous council; ICBF agreement with Gitó Dokabú resguardo; pilot with 296 youth; no dated trigger or resguardo-level figures, flagged low promise. [La FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/colombia/hasta-con-bebedizos-menores-indigenas-en-risaralda-estan-atentando-contra-sus-vidas); [ICBF](https://www.icbf.gov.co/noticias/icbf-promueve-garantia-derechos-en-comunidades-etnicas-de-risaralda)
column7: Not studied in economics; clinical literature only (Pereira ICU case series)
column8: Do illegal-economy or armed-confinement shocks raise youth suicidal behavior? No clear variation and very small N; SIVIGILA 356 (with ethnicity), Vital Statistics.

column5: Clan del Golfo armed strike after "Otoniel" extradition (Colombia, 5-10 May 2022)
column6: Halted social, economic and school activity; classes suspended in Córdoba on 6-May (>60 schools); Indepaz counted 127 actions in 73 municipalities of 10 departments (119 or 178 in other counts, nv); replica: ELN strike in Chocó Feb-2025. [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/colombia/indepaz-entrego-balance-del-paro-armado-del-clan-del-golfo-418719); [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/noticias/2022/05/06/alarma-por-paro-armado-en-el-caribe-suspenden-transporte-clases-y-comercio-en-varios-departamentos/)
column7: Not studied as an event (top-5 case); only general conflict-education work (Munévar, Silva and Sarmiento)
column8: Does a 3-5 day armed lockdown affect attendance, dropout, enrollment, Saber 11 and informal income? Exogenous extradition date; affected vs unaffected municipalities in same department; stacked with ELN strikes; SIMAT, daily SIEDCO, Vital Statistics.

column5: Shottas-Espartanos gang truce in Buenaventura (Colombia, Oct-2022 to 2025)
column6: Began 1-Oct-2022 and removed "invisible borders"; ~90 days without inter-gang homicides by Dec-2022; extended to Feb-2025; 2025 breakdown with >50 homicides vs ~5 per month in 2024; "zero killings" claim inexact. [La Marea](https://lamarea.com/2023/01/11/buenaventura-de-ser-una-de-las-ciudades-mas-violentas-del-mundo-a-celebrar-100-dias-en-paz); [Cambio](https://cambiocolombia.com/pais/en-buenaventura-eso-de-cero-asesinatos-durante-la-tregua-no-resulto-tan-cierto-kyle-johnson); [PARES](https://www.pares.com.co/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/informe-octubre.pdf)
column7: Not studied (truce); invisible borders little studied, qualitative only (Medellín covered by Haugan)
column8: Did removing invisible borders cut dropout and absenteeism and raise Saber 11 in border-neighborhood schools, and did it reverse after the breakdown? On (2022) and off (2025) for the same population; synthetic control with Tumaco, Quibdó; SIMAT by school.

column5: Shopkeeper extortion and Los Costeños-Los Pepes truce in Barranquilla (Colombia, 2022-2026)
column6: 336 extortion reports in 2022; 668 from 1-Jan to 25-Jul-2025; truce signed 2-Oct-2025, extended to 20-Jan-2026; first month -57% homicides, -84% extortion (MinDefensa), but Police attribute only 17% of the drop to the truce. [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/bogota/2025/10/03/lideres-de-bandas-criminales-los-costenos-y-los-pepes-firmaron-tregua-en-la-paz-de-petro/); [La Silla Vacía](https://www.lasillavacia.com/silla-nacional/caribe/en-barranquilla-bajan-los-homicidios-pero-no-por-la-tregua/)
column7: Little studied; CESED descriptive business-victimization surveys
column8: Do extortion waves and their pause affect microbusiness survival, informality, teen work and school attendance? Event study on truce start, expiry and Dec-2023 ceasefire; neighborhood SIEDCO intensity; synthetic control with Cartagena, Santa Marta; business registry, GEIH.

column5: Hurricane Iota in Providencia (Colombia, 16-Nov-2020)
column6: ~98% of infrastructure destroyed; only 615 of 961 students enrolled in 2020 re-enrolled in 2021; Nov-2021: 37 temporary classrooms for 960 students; schools still not rebuilt; unstudied replica: Mocoa 2017 (12,000-12,500 students without class). [MEN](https://www.mineducacion.gov.co:443/1780/articles-413462_recurso_505.pdf); [Radio Nacional](https://www.radionacional.co/regiones/providencia/huracan-iota-entrega-aulas-provisionales); [OCHA](https://reliefweb.int/report/colombia/colombia-co-mocoa-avalanche-humanitarian-situation-report-5-19-april-2017)
column7: Not studied in economics; INS cross-sectional health study, qualitative gender book
column8: Did total destruction and slow rebuilding affect school retention, Saber 11 and Raizal out-migration? Extreme (Providencia), moderate (San Andrés) and island or mainland controls; SIMAT student panel; stack with Mocoa; COVID confound.

column5: Short-term rental restriction in Medellín (Colombia, announced 12-Mar-2024)
column6: Mayor proposed banning short-term rentals in family buildings after a sexual-exploitation case; El Poblado had 4,241 tourist dwellings (Jul-2024); land-use plan (POT) review Sep-2026. [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/medellin/2024/03/13/polemica-por-propuesta-de-alcalde-de-medellin-de-no-permitir-el-uso-de-apartamentos-para-rentas-cortas-ni-airbnb/); [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/medellin/prohiben-renta-corta-en-urbanizacion-de-el-poblado-por-casos-de-explotacion-sexual-NI25691387)
column7: Partly explained: rents studied (Fonseca Galvis and Giraldo 2026, no causal rent effect); families with children and 2024 restriction not studied
column8: Residual question: did the restriction change the composition of households with children near public schools? Announcement date and building-level bans (hard to observe); scraped Airbnb or AirDNA, SIMAT, Medellín Quality of Life Survey.

column5: ETCR former FARC zones and neighboring veredas (Colombia, 2017 onward)
column6: Former FARC transition zones set up in 2017, with later relocations and abandonments; the count (~24) comes from researcher memory, unsourced (nv). [El País Cali](https://www.elpais.com.co/proceso-de-paz/informe-advierte-sobre-reincorporacion-e-implementacion-del-acuerdo-de-paz.html); [FIP](https://storage.ideaspaz.org/documents/FIP_ReincorporacionFARC_web_FINAL.pdf)
column7: Little studied; qualitative only (aggregate Peace Agreement effect excluded)
column8: Did an ETCR change enrollment, attendance and health services in nearby veredas? Distance rings before and after 2017, relocations and closures as second date; location negotiated (endogenous); ARN coordinates, SIMAT, REPS/RIPS, Saber 11.

column5: Direct administration of SGP transfers by indigenous resguardos (Colombia, 2014 onward)
column6: Decrees 1953 and 2719 of 2014: DNP-certified resguardos manage their own allocation (0.52% of SGP), otherwise the municipality does; Comptroller probed ~COP 800,000M (761,000M per Blu Radio) sent to Cauca without visible gains (date 2019 or 2026, nv). [Blu Radio](https://www.bluradio.com/nacion/donde-estan-los-millonarios-recursos-que-gobierno-gira-a-indigenas-en-cauca); [DNP Kit Étnico](https://colaboracion.dnp.gov.co/CDT/Desarrollo%20Territorial/Portal%20Territorial/KitEtnico/DECRETO1082.pdf)
column7: Not studied (top-5 case); only a descriptive UNAD thesis on Popayán
column8: Do indigenous schooling, maternal-child health and nutrition improve when the resguardo manages its own allocation? Staggered DiD on certification dates vs not-yet-certified resguardos; certification list via DNP petition; SICODIS, Saber 11 and Vital Statistics with ethnicity.

column5: Atrato River declared a subject of rights, ruling T-622 (Colombia, Nov-2016)
column6: Court ordered toxicological studies on mercury; precedent: complaint over deaths of 37 children in Chocó in 2016 (cause disputed); CGR audit in 2019. [ANLA](https://www.anla.gov.co/wanla/eureka/jurisprudencia/sentencias/sentencia-t-622-de-2016-de-la-corte-constitucional-rio-atrato-como-entidad-sujeto-de-derechos); [News24](https://www.news24.com/world/news/investigation-into-deaths-of-37-colombian-children-20160205)
column7: Partly explained: mining-to-newborn-health mechanism studied (Romero and Saavedra 2016, DiD); the ruling itself not studied
column8: Did the ruling change neonatal health in riverside municipalities vs other Pacific mining basins? Ruling date × ~15 basin municipalities vs mining municipalities outside, EVOA mining intensity; Vital Statistics, SIVIGILA 390; null effect likely.

column5: Coal dust and the Wayuu resguardo of Provincial, ruling T-614 (Colombia, 16-Dec-2019)
column6: Ruling set PM2.5 targets of 25 µg/m3 daily and 10 monthly; neighboring event: Arroyo Bruno diversion (SU-698/2017); Comptroller said in Feb-2023 that rulings were not being met. [Corte Constitucional](https://www.corteconstitucional.gov.co/relatoria/2019/T-614-19.htm); [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2023/02/14/autoridades-ambientales-no-cumplen-sentencias-en-el-arroyo-bruno-advierte-contraloria/)
column7: Little studied; Viloria de la Hoz (1998) without health; Pimiento et al. (2024), method nv
column8: Did coal-dust exposure worsen child respiratory health and birth outcomes downwind, and improve after T-614? Wind direction × distance to pit × monthly output; few treated units; RIPS, Vital Statistics, SISAIRE, ANM production.

column5: Multipurpose cadastre updates (Colombia, 2019/2020 to 2026)
column6: Per IGAC as cited in press, 326 municipalities updated by Feb-2026 (~40% of territory); warnings of "exorbitant" property-tax hikes in >200 municipalities. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/gobierno/que-esta-pasando-con-la-actualizacion-catastral-que-se-adelanta-en-colombia-626683); [RTVC](https://www.rtvcnoticias.com/colombia/petro-cuestiona-paro-civico-por-catastro-multiproposito-y-aclara-impacto-en-impuesto)
column7: Little studied on fiscal side (Muñoz-Mora, Almonacid and Peña 2026); not studied for human development
column8: Does the property-tax jump trigger land sales, formalization or changes in labor supply and schooling of peasant households? Staggered DiD by update year × appraisal jump; tax-exempt resguardos as within-municipality contrast; IGAC, FUT/CHIP, SIMAT, rural GEIH.

column5: IPSE electrification in Non-Interconnected Zones (Colombia, 2025)
column6: 24-hour service for 1,334 users in 59 Wayuu communities of Manaure (Jun-2025 note); 94 hybrid systems in six Puerto Carreño communities (date nv); 60.45% of non-telemetered ZNI localities had 5-7 hours of service per day. [MinEnergía](https://www.minenergia.gov.co/es/sala-de-prensa/noticias-index/por-primera-vez-ind%C3%ADgenas-wayuu-de-la-guajira-acceder%C3%A1n-al-servicio-de-energ%C3%ADa-las-24-horas-del-d%C3%ADa/); [Radio Nacional](https://radionacional.co/noticias-colombia/59-comunidades-wayuu-tendran-energia-247-anuncia-presidente-petro)
column7: Little studied; 3SLS on electrified households only (CET 2018), IDB multi-country review
column8: Does moving from ~5 to 24 hours of power raise school attendance, Saber 11 and female work in indigenous localities? Service start by locality and monthly telemetry hours (intensive margin); IPSE/CNM telemetry on datos.gov.co, georeferenced SIMAT.

column5: Peasant Reserve Zones (ZRC) (Colombia, 2022-2025)
column6: Four approved at COP16 (Oct-2024); ANT Observatory counted 20 ZRC covering 1,536,314.9 ha in Jul-2025, 14 under the Petro government (counts conflict); Sumapaz by ANT Agreement 252/2022. [Observatorio de la ANT](https://observatorio.ant.gov.co/sites/default/files/2025-07/documentos/archivos/territorialidades_dgops.pdf); [Agronegocios](https://www.agronegocios.co/agricultura/nueva-zona-de-reserva-campesina-en-antioquia-4291216)
column7: Little studied on deforestation (Gutiérrez-Vélez et al. 2022 abstract); not studied on welfare
column8: Do schooling or youth migration change in veredas inside a ZRC vs neighboring ones? Spatial discontinuity at polygon borders × designation date; older ZRCs give a longer horizon (dates nv); ANT polygons, CNA 2014, Census 2018, SIMAT.

column5: Agrarian reform land purchases (Colombia, 2023-2025; low-promise extra candidate)
column6: 634,798 ha and 2,705 properties purchased by 15-Jul-2025, vs 712,205 ha in another balance; figures not comparable; no academic verification done. [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/economia/el-gobierno-nacional-alcanzo-las-634-798-hectareas-de-tierras-compradas-hasta-julio-4207276); [Agronegocios](https://www.agronegocios.co/agricultura/implementacion-de-reforma-agraria-a-cierre-de-2025-4299775)
column7: Not studied (no academic search reported; low promise)
column8: Low promise per source; any study of land-purchase effects on recipient households would first need dated, property-level purchase records and a reconciliation of the conflicting hectare figures.

column5: La Línea Tunnel opening (Colombia, 2020; low-promise extra candidate)
column6: Major road tunnel opened in 2020; only accessibility studies found; very few municipalities treated. [DYNA](https://revistas.unal.edu.co/index.php/dyna/article/view/119743)
column7: Little studied; accessibility studies only (DYNA)
column8: Low promise per source: a before-after comparison of municipalities served by the tunnel is possible in principle, but very few treated municipalities limit statistical power.

column5: OCCRE residency control in San Andrés (Colombia, ongoing; low-promise extra candidate)
column6: Island residency and circulation control body; no dated threshold identified; only legal works found. [UNAL](https://revistas.unal.edu.co/index.php/ccaribe/article/download/64165/59443/325846)
column7: Not studied in economics; legal works only
column8: Low promise per source: without a dated threshold or rule change there is no clean variation to exploit.

column5: Prior consultation (consulta previa) with ethnic communities (Colombia, ongoing; low-promise extra candidate)
column6: Average consultation duration ~6 months. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/la-importancia-de-las-consultas-previa-para-la-ejecucion-de-proyectos-581353)
column7: Little studied
column8: Low promise per source: variation in consultation duration across projects exists, but the natural outcome is measured per project (delays, costs), not in human development.

column5: "Muévete a la U" university transport subsidy (Colombia, Apr 2023–2026; Atlántico, excluding Barranquilla)
column6: Ordinance approved 28-Apr-2023; first call Jul–Aug 2023; covers 22 of 23 municipalities, explicitly excluding Barranquilla; paused 2024, reactivated 2025-2. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/atlantico/2023/04/28/asamblea-aprueba-proyecto-para-subsidiar-transporte-a-estudiantes-universitarios-de-municipios-del-atlantico-996815/); [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/regional/2023/09/02/mas-de-3000-estudiantes-seran-beneficiados-con-auxilio-de-transporte/)
column7: Not studied. Closest: IDB paper on Medellín school transport subsidy (authors nv).
column8: Does an attendance-conditioned transport subsidy raise retention and graduation of peripheral-municipality students? Spatial DiD (Soledad, Malambo, Puerto Colombia vs. Barranquilla, pre/post 2023-2) with SPADIES/SNIES, Saber 11/Pro and beneficiary lists by petition.

column5: "Mi Casa Avanza" housing-improvement lotteries, Corvivienda (Colombia, May 2024–2026; Cartagena)
column6: Public ball-draw lotteries: El Líbano 29-May-2024 (Res. 232, 141 subsidies); Bayunca Jun-2024 (90); Isla Fuerte Jul-2025 (40); Res. 148 Apr-2026 (1,290 slots). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/cartagena/2024/05/29/este-29-de-mayo-se-escogeran-los-beneficiarios-de-mi-casa-avanza-en-el-libano/); [Corvivienda Res. 232](https://corvivienda.gov.co/repositorio/2024/mi_casa_avanza/RESOLUCION%20No.%20232%20DEL%2005%20DE%20JUNIO%20DE%202024%20ASIGNACI%C3%93N%20DE%20141%20SUBSIDIOS%20-%20LIBANO.pdf)
column7: Not studied. Analogue only: Piso Firme (Cattaneo et al., 2009; nv).
column8: Do sanitation and housing upgrades reduce child diarrhea/respiratory infections and school absence? Within-neighborhood lottery across several rounds, using published Corvivienda draw records plus RIPS, SIMAT and SISBEN IV via agreement.

column5: De facto suspension of 50% Metrolínea fare subsidy (Colombia, Jan–Dec 2024, reopened Nov-2025; Bucaramanga)
column6: Subsidy suspended throughout 2024; reopened 13-Nov-2025 with a target of 40,000 (up from about 8,000); "reactivated" 10-Mar-2026. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/area-metropolitana/bucaramanga/2024/06/28/subsidio-en-el-pasaje-del-sitm-metrolinea-no-tiene-fecha-de-reinicio/); [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/area-metropolitana/bucaramanga/2025/11/13/en-bucaramanga-transporte-masivo-otorgara-beneficios-del-50-en-pasaje-diario/)
column7: Not studied. Only an untitled UIS document (nv).
column8: Does temporary loss of a fare subsidy cut trips, university attendance and elderly health-service use? Individual event study around suspension and reactivation, using operator card validations (petition) and SPADIES.

column5: "Renta Básica" of Medellín Futuro (Colombia, 2020–2023; Medellín)
column6: Promised to 91,485 families with 10.5% fulfilment; Aug-2021 cycle reached about 73,139 families; single 2022 payment to 30,904. [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/antioquia/asi-analizan-los-mas-pobres-lo-que-ha-pasado-con-las-promesas-de-ayuda-de-la-alcaldia-ON17293940); [Alcaldía de Medellín](https://www.medellin.gov.co/es/sala-de-prensa/noticias/mas-de-73-000-familias-se-benefician-con-el-pago-de-otro-ciclo-de-renta-basica/)
column7: Little studied. Descriptive Uniandes Escuela de Gobierno DT-90 (authors nv).
column8: What do small, irregular municipal transfers do to food consumption and political trust? Exploit coverage changes across cycles and possible SISBEN cutoffs (nv), with cycle lists via petition and Medellín Quality of Life Survey.

column5: Municipal "minimum vital water" free allowances (Colombia, 2013–2025; Manizales, Bucaramanga, Cali, Pasto)
column6: Manizales 2017 bill with SISBEN cutoff of 25 points (approval date nv); Bucaramanga Acuerdo 032/2013; Cali Acuerdo 370/2014; Pasto Acuerdo 033/2019. [LA FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/colombia/concejo-manizales-aprueba-minimo-vital-agua); [Concejo de Pasto](https://www.concejodepasto.gov.co/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Acuerdo-033-Agua-Potable-2019.pdf)
column7: Little studied. Ex-ante simulation, Semestre Económico (2011).
column8: Does a free water quota raise consumption, cut arrears disconnections and child diarrhea? RD at Manizales SISBEN 25-point cutoff plus staggered DiD by city adoption date, using utility billing (petition), SUI, RIPS and vital statistics.

column5: LPG cylinder subsidy and its payment arrears (Colombia, 2013–2025; Nariño, Putumayo and 4 other departments)
column6: 2013 pilot (Res. 90855), later 6 departments; strata 1 (50%) and 2 (40%); cap raised 9-Nov-2023; distributors unpaid since Jul-2024. [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/colombia/suspension-del-subsidio-al-glp-en-cilindros-devolveria-a-miles-de-colombianos-a-la-lena/); [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/energia/gobierno-adeuda-93-184-millones-en-subsidios-al-glp-y-crece-la-preocupacion-por-mas-de-un-millon-de-usuarios-496444)
column7: Not studied. Only design/comparison theses (U. Distrital, Uniremington).
column8: Did non-payment raise effective cylinder prices and push households back to firewood, with respiratory effects? DiD covered departments vs. neighbors and by stratum around Nov-2023 and Jul-2024, using DANE ECV, RIPS/SISPRO, SUI and CREG prices.

column5: Cut in electricity "subsistence consumption" block (Colombia, 2005–2007; nationwide, altitude threshold 1,000 masl)
column6: UPME Res. 355/2004 cut the subsidized block from 200 to 173 kWh below 1,000 masl and to 130 kWh above, phased 2005–2007; no contemporary press, only the regulation. [CREG](https://gestornormativo.creg.gov.co/gestor/entorno/docs/resolucion_upme_0355_2004.htm)
column7: Little studied. Santamaría (2023), descriptive; McRae dissertation (use of threshold nv).
column8: How much did strata 1–2 consumption fall when the subsidized block shrank, and is there bunching at the kink? Intensity DiD (70 vs. 27 kWh cut), geographic RD at 1,000 masl, bunching, using public SUI by municipality-stratum.

column5: Family-allowance cash benefit (cuota monetaria) eligibility notch (Colombia, ongoing, 2022–2026 amounts; nationwide by department)
column6: Lost above 4 minimum wages; household cap 6 minimum wages; amounts set yearly by department (2022: $31,281–$63,410; 2024: $40,446–$85,574); 15% rural surcharge (legal basis nv). [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/finanzas/subsidio-cajas-de-compensacion-2022-asi-sera-la-cuota-monetaria-por-departamentos-561716); [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/economia/finanzas-personales/subsidio-monetario-2026-quienes-pueden-recibirlo-y-cuanto-se-paga-noticias-colombia/)
column7: Little studied. Descriptive only (SSF Observatory; Farné and Carrasco González).
column8: Does the 4-minimum-wage notch cause wage bunching or underreporting in PILA, and do amounts affect fertility or formality? Kleven-Waseem notch plus yearly department-by-fund variation, using restricted PILA and public annual communiqués.

column5: Jóvenes en Paz transfers (Colombia, Nov 2023–2026; nationwide)
column6: Decree 1649 of 22-Nov-2023: up to COP 1 million/month; court refused suspension Sep-2024; 2026 payment calendar redone for delays; Apr-2026 cycles of 12,623 and 9,593 beneficiaries. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2024/09/20/los-beneficiarios-del-programa-jovenes-en-paz-no-perderan-sus-pagos-tribunal-nego-propuesta-de-congresistas-que-pedian-suspender-las-transferencias/); [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/finanzas/prosperidad-social-redefine-pagos-de-jovenes-en-paz-para-estabilizar-giros-y-superar-retrasos-operativos-491029)
column7: Not studied. Only an MEN call for implementers, not an evaluation.
column8: Did transfers reduce victimization and criminal involvement, and did payment delays hurt retention? Staggered municipal rollout, DNP targeting score (possible RD), age 14–28 limit, using public cycle counts, SIEDCO and nominal lists via agreement.

column5: FOSFEC unemployment protection mechanism (Colombia, 2013–2022; nationwide, by compensation fund)
column6: Replaced FONEDE (Dec. 2113/2013; Law 1636/2013); 2020 emergency benefits (Dec. 488, 770, 801); ended by Res. 2416/2022; waiting lists in each fund. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/economia/nacional/2023/10/05/gobierno-presentara-una-propuesta-para-crear-un-subsidio-universal-para-el-desempleo-ante-cajas-de-compensacion-familiar/); [Res. 2416 de 2022](https://normograma.icfes.gov.co/docs/pdf/resolucion_mtra_2416_2022.pdf)
column7: Little studied. Vélez (2021), UNAL thesis using PSM.
column8: Does FOSFEC access lengthen unemployment or improve formal re-employment quality? Waiting-list order within funds, 2020 expansion and 2022 end, using restricted PILA, fund applicant records and GEIH.

column5: Elderly-welfare stamp tax and Centros Vida (Colombia, 2023–2026; several municipalities)
column6: Low execution (17.68% in Dosquebradas, 2024); local comptroller findings; Law 2581 of 1-Jun-2026 changes earmarking. [Semana](https://www.semana.com/nacion/pereira/articulo/algunos-centros-vida-de-pereira-se-encuentran-enredados-por-presuntas-irregularidades-esta-es-la-denuncia/202325/); [El País Cali](https://www.elpais.com.co/cali/y-la-plata-de-los-abuelos-las-irregularidades-que-encontro-la-contraloria-en-el-ancianato-san-miguel.html)
column7: Not studied. Only management monographs (Ulloa Rodríguez, Facatativá).
column8: Does stamp revenue translate into Centros Vida coverage and fewer elderly hospitalizations or deaths? Ordinance-set tax rates, departmental allocation rules and the Law 2581 change, using public FUT/CHIP, SECOP and SISPRO.

column5: Rural school connectivity delay in "Region B" after Centros Poblados scandal (Colombia, 2021–2022; ~15 departments)
column6: Contract voided 2021; Res. 703 of 18-May-2022 reassigned Region B to ETB NET while Region A (Comcel) proceeded; regions fixed in 2020 tender. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/colombia/2021/12/16/mintic-etb-y-skynet-asumiran-contrato-de-centros-poblados-873651/); [Noticias Caracol](https://www.noticiascaracol.com/colombia/a-boyaca-llego-centros-poblados-con-equipos-pero-sin-conectividad)
column7: Not studied. Closest: home internet and Saber 11 via 2SLS, SAGE Open (2021).
column8: What did a 1–3 year school connectivity delay do to Saber 3/5/9/11, enrollment and dropout? Region A vs. Region B (pre-scandal partition), staggered rollout and department borders, using school lists, ICFES by school, C-600 and SIMAT.

column5: Crisis and intervention of Fundación Universitaria San Martín (Colombia, 2013–2016; 17 cities)
column6: MEN suspended admissions in 2013; 20,000–26,000 students affected; 1,056 transferred to 30 institutions. [Semana](https://www.semana.com/mineducacion-presenta-rendicion-de-cuentas-sobre-la-san-martin/454437-3/); [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/colombia/tenemos-la-facultad-de-cerrar-la-san-martin-pero-esa-no-es-la-decision-236222)
column7: Not studied. Only legal analyses of Law 1740.
column8: How does a private university collapse affect students' dropout, graduation, Saber Pro and labor-market entry? Pre/post-2013 cohorts vs. similar institutions and suspended vs. non-suspended programs, using SPADIES, SNIES, Saber Pro and OLE.

column5: Universidad Autónoma del Caribe crisis and special oversight (Colombia, 2017–2018; Barranquilla)
column6: Financial crisis from mid-2017; special oversight by Res. 0001962 of 12-Feb-2018 (Law 1740); indefinite strike from 21-Feb-2018; staff fell from 1,034 to 773. [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/educacion/2018/02/21/profesores-y-estudiantes-de-uniautonoma-se-declaran-en-paro-indefinido/); [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/barranquilla/2023/01/22/uniautonoma-que-es-lo-que-esta-pasando-en-su-interior-972259/)
column7: Not studied. No economic work; legal documents only.
column8: Does special oversight slow or accelerate dropout, and where does demand shift? Staggered event study of institutions under Law 1740 plus spillovers to local competitors, using SNIES, SPADIES, Saber Pro and MEN resolutions.

column5: Local strikes at public universities (Colombia, 2016–2021; Uniatlántico, Barranquilla; U. del Tolima, Ibagué)
column6: Uniatlántico strike from 25-Oct-2019, 2019-II semester suspended, normal from Feb-2020, new strike May-2021; U. del Tolima closed Feb-2016, hunger strike 6–15 Jul-2016. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/barranquilla/2019/10/25/estudiantes-de-ua-votan-paro-tras-tensa-jornada-675348/); [Global Voices](https://globalvoices.org/2016/08/02/the-successful-hunger-strike-that-changed-colombias-university-of-tolima/)
column7: Not studied. Only a qualitative dropout study (Unillanos).
column8: How much do prolonged semester suspensions raise dropout and graduation delays, and does demand shift to private institutions or SENA? Exposed vs. earlier cohorts and vs. non-striking public universities, using SPADIES, SNIES, Saber Pro.

column5: Caregato dike breach and flooded schools (Colombia, Aug 2021–2026; La Mojana, Sucre)
column6: About 25,000 students affected and 58 schools under water in Sucre; recurrent flooding through 2026. [Radio Nacional](https://radionacional.co/noticias-colombia/inundaciones-en-la-mojana-sucrena-25-mil-estudiantes-afectados); [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/sucre/2023/01/19/ades-alerta-sobre-desercion-escolar-en-el-sur-de-sucre-971725/)
column7: Little studied. Muñoz-Morales (2025, EDCC) on 2010 floods, not Caregato.
column8: What is the effect of losing a school site for several years vs. a transitory rain shock? Schools inside vs. outside flood extent (Sentinel/IDEAM) with varying duration, using C-600, ICFES, SIMAT and georeferenced schools.

column5: Official school transport failed to start (Colombia, Feb–Mar 2025; Cali)
column6: Service did not start 24-Feb-2025 for 21,000+ students; emergency contract of COP 2,115 million for 701 routes; resumed 25-Feb; 4-Mar-2025 contract for 22,700 students. [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/cali/2025/02/24/no-iniciara-servicio-de-transporte-escolare-en-cali-esto-dijo-secretaria-de-educacion/); [El País Cali](https://www.elpais.com.co/cali/mas-de-2-mil-millones-se-destinaron-para-contratar-el-servicio-de-transporte-escolar-en-cali-durante-la-urgencia-manifiesta-2547.html)
column7: Not studied (weak verification).
column8: Does disrupting school transport at year start reduce attendance and raise rural dropout? Route vs. non-route students in the same school, plus panel of territorial entities by SECOP II contract date vs. calendar start, using SIMAT and C-600.

column5: Chain closures of obstetric wards (Colombia, 2024–2026; Medellín/Antioquia and Bogotá)
column6: Antioquia had 1,049 obstetric beds in 2012; Medellín: 6 clinics closed, 7 remain (Mar-2025); Clínica del Prado cuts 30 beds (Feb-2026); Bogotá: San Ignacio (late 2024), Clínica de Occidente (21-Apr-2025). [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/medellin/camas-partos-nacimientos-medellin-hospitales-cierran-servicios-MG26758589); [La República](https://www.larepublica.co/empresas/clinica-de-occidente-cerrara-sus-servicios-de-obstetricia-y-neonatologia-el-21-de-abril-4099932)
column7: Not studied for Colombia. Abroad: Malouf et al. (2020, BMJ Open).
column8: Does closure of the nearest delivery ward raise non-institutional births, low birth weight and neonatal mortality? Staggered event study using REPS closure dates and travel distance, controlling for falling births, with public vital statistics microdata.

column5: Shortage of monthly injectable contraceptives (Colombia, ~Oct–Nov 2019, date nv; nationwide)
column6: Femelin, Cyclofem and Cyclofemina out of stock due to manufacturing failures. [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/salud/las-razones-detras-de-la-escasez-de-tres-anticonceptivos-en-colombia-article-892262/) (date nv); [El Tiempo](https://www.eltiempo.com/salud/anticonceptivos-agotados-cuales-son-las-alternativas-685303)
column7: Not studied.
column8: Did the disruption raise unplanned pregnancies and births 9–11 months later, especially among adolescents and the subsidized regime? Shortage date × prior department injectable use (ENDS 2015, RIPS), short pre-COVID window, with vital statistics reconstructing conception month.

column5: Prodeco (Glencore) relinquishes coal titles (Colombia, Feb–Sep 2021; La Jagua de Ibirico, El Paso, Becerril, Cesar)
column6: Prodeco renounced titles 4-Feb-2021; ANM accepted 3 titles 3-Sep-2021. [Forbes](https://forbes.co/2021/02/04/negocios/el-grupo-prodeco-renuncia-a-sus-minas-de-carbon-en-colombia/); [La FM](https://www.lafm.com.co/economia/desempleo-en-colombia-prodeco-renuncia-a-titulos-mineros-236606); [Asuntos Legales](https://www.asuntoslegales.com.co/actualidad/contraloria-hara-un-seguimiento-especial-a-problemas-generados-por-cierre-de-minas-3598016)
column7: Little studied. Theses (UNAD, UFPS) and SEI (2024) just-transition report.
column8: What happened to formal employment, wages and informality of displaced workers and their municipalities? Event study (Mar–Apr 2020, Feb-2021), treated vs. Drummond/Cerrejón coal municipalities, tracking workers by firm ID in restricted PILA plus GEIH and SGR royalties.

column5: Replacement of animal-drawn carts (carreteros) (Colombia, 2013–2015 and 2026; Bogotá, Girón)
column6: District Decree 040/2013; first handover 6-Mar-2013; 2,890 censused; about 1,000 not replaced per Council (2015); 2026 Court struck tourism exception (Girón). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/2013/01/25/bogota-quiere-erradicar-los-vehiculos-de-traccion-animal-o-carromulas/); [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2026/09/24/desde-giron-la-corte-constitucional-tomo-historica-decision-sobre-la-traccion-animal-en-el-turismo/)
column7: Not studied in quantitative economics. USTA (2015) process study; WIEGO brief.
column8: Does an occupational ban compensated with physical capital change income, formality and staying in recycling? Eligibility census with cutoff, non-replaced eligibles as controls, city-specific dates, using SDM census (petition), RUNT, UAESP RURO, SISBEN.

column5: Special Economic and Social Zones, ZESE (Colombia, Dec 2019 onward; La Guajira, Norte de Santander, Arauca, Armenia, Quibdó)
column6: Law 1955/2019 art. 268 and Decree 2112 (Dec-2019): 0% income tax for 5 years conditional on job creation. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/las-5-regiones-especiales-para-atraer-inversion-535948); [DIAN](https://www.dian.gov.co/Prensa/Paginas/NG-Regimen-Especial-en-Materia-Tributaria-Zona-Economica-y-Social-Especial-Zese.aspx)
column7: Little studied. Descriptive Unisimón thesis on Cúcuta; qualitative analysis.
column8: Did the incentive create firms and formal jobs, or only relocate firms or change tax IDs? Administrative borders (Armenia vs. rest of Quindío, Quibdó vs. Chocó), bunching in 3-year incorporation window, unemployment criterion RD, using RUES, PILA, DIAN.

column5: Informal fuel sellers (pimpineros): reconversion program and border closure supply cut (Colombia, 2010–2015; Cúcuta)
column6: Reconversion program 2010–2014; supply cut by 19-Aug-2015 border closure (closure itself excluded; only occupational margin). [Semana](https://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/economia-de-cucuta-es-afectada-por-cierre-de-frontera/439947-3); [Forbes](https://forbes.co/2020/10/17/negocios/apoyan-emprendimientos-de-pimpineros-para-que-no-vendan-combustible-de-contrabando/)
column7: Little studied. Theses (Externado, UFPS) and an ESAP article.
column8: What happened to fuel sellers' jobs and income, and did reconversion prevent shifts to illicit activity? Aug-2015 shock in high vs. low dependence municipalities with fuel quota as dose, using Cúcuta GEIH and MinMinas/UPME quotas; confounded by Venezuelan migration.

column5: Weekly social-security contributions for domestic workers and service bonus (Colombia, Nov 2013 and Jul 2016; nationwide)
column6: Decree 2616 (Nov-2013) allowed contributions by weeks; Law 1788 (Jul-2016) granted service bonus; 8 in 10 domestic workers still lack the bonus (2025). [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/2016/07/12/mintrabajo-celebro-sancion-de-la-ley-que-otorga-primas-al-servicio-domestico/); [Forbes](https://forbes.co/2025/06/13/actualidad/ocho-de-cada-diez-trabajadoras-del-hogar-siguen-sin-recibir-la-prima-en-colombia)
column7: Little studied (subject to verification). U. del Rosario policy paper; EAFIT and Univalle theses (nv).
column8: Did lowering fixed costs of formalizing day work raise affiliation, and did Law 1788 reduce it? Pre/post Nov-2013 and Jul-2016, part-time vs. full-time domestic vs. other low-income occupations, using public GEIH and restricted PILA.

column5: 120% tax deduction for hiring older adults without pension (Colombia, Jul 2020 onward; nationwide)
column6: Law 2040 of 27-Jul-2020 grants 120% deduction; take-up of the incentive unknown. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/ley-2040-promueve-empleo-para-adultos-mayores-sin-pension-543119); [Asuntos Legales](https://www.asuntoslegales.com.co/consultorio/incentivos-para-la-contratacion-laboral-de-adultos-mayores-3100962)
column7: Not studied (incomplete verification).
column8: Does the deduction raise formal employment near pension age or only subsidize inframarginal hires? Age-threshold DiD from Jul-2020 (age threshold nv in law text), using restricted PILA and DIAN plus GEIH.

column5: Record deportations from the US (Colombia, 2025; nationwide, origin municipalities)
column6: Diplomatic standoff 26–28 Jan-2025; 201 deportees arrived 28-Jan; 23,045 expelled in 2025; RUR programs and Antioquia jobs plan. [Cancillería](https://www.cancilleria.gov.co/en/node/30109); [El Colombiano](https://www.elcolombiano.com/colombia/deportaciones-colombianos-desde-ee-uu-aumento-en-2025-por-trump-NO28620184)
column7: Little studied. Medina (U. Liège), descriptive, pre-2025.
column8: Did the deportation shock raise unemployment and informality or cut remittances in origin municipalities? Predetermined exposure (US emigration in 2005/2018 censuses, remittances) × 2025 national jump, using BanRep remittances, GEIH and Migración Colombia aggregates.

column5: UK visa waiver for Colombians and its reversal (Colombia, Nov 2022–Nov 2024; UK-bound migration)
column6: Visa exemption from 9-Nov-2022; reversal announced 26-Nov-2024. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/colombia/2024/11/26/a-partir-de-que-fecha-rige-la-nueva-exigencia-de-visa-para-ingresar-a-reino-unido/); [Home Office HC 334](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6745970eb58081a2d9be9686/E03247522_-__HC_334__-_EXPLANATORY_MEMORANDUM__Print_Ready_.pdf)
column7: Not studied. No paper, working paper or thesis found.
column8: Does opening a legal entry route raise emigration and asylum, and does closing it reverse or divert flows to Spain/Germany? On-off DiD vs. nationalities still requiring visas, using Home Office quarterly asylum data, Eurostat migr_asyappctzm, Migración Colombia exits.

column5: ELN armed strikes in the Baudó (Colombia, Aug 2021, Nov 2023, Mar 2026; Chocó)
column6: Nov-2023: 714 family units, about 3,000 displaced; 17–23 Mar-2026: 6,000+ confined; precedent Aug-2021. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2023/11/07/desplazamiento-de-casi-3000-personas-dejo-el-paro-armado-del-eln/); [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/noticias/2026/03/23/defensoria-confirma-el-fin-del-paro-armado-del-eln-en-choco-pero-advierte-las-comunidades-siguen-con-miedo/)
column7: Little studied (event not; displacement generally yes). Ibáñez and Vélez (2005), CEDE; none on confinement.
column8: How does days-long confinement vs. displacement affect school attendance, nutrition, health and local prices? Event study with exact start/end dates vs. unaffected Chocó neighbors and recurrence, using RUV, OCHA/Defensoría, SIMAT and SISPRO.

column5: Return Law (Ley Retorno) incentives (Colombia, 2012 and 2021 reform; nationwide)
column6: Law 1565/2012: one-time customs and tax incentives for those 3+ years abroad; reformed by Law 2136/2021; PL 528 of 2026 (nv); documented only in regulations, no dated press. [DIAN](https://www.dian.gov.co/aduanas/Paginas/Beneficios-de-la-Ley-de-Retorno.aspx); [Función Pública](https://funcionpublica.gov.co/eva/gestornormativo/norma.php?i=48662)
column7: Little studied. Qualitative Revista Austral (2019); probit in Gerencia (2022, nv).
column8: Did incentives raise return of skilled or capital-holding migrants, or subsidize inframarginal returns? Discontinuity at 3 years abroad, bunching at 17,130 UVT threshold, 2012 and 2021 events, using CIR certificates (petition), DIAN C180/C181, GEIH, Census 2018.

column5: Emberá displaced in Parque Nacional and returns (Colombia, Sep 2021–Sep 2025; Bogotá to Risaralda and Chocó)
column6: Encampment Sep-2021 to Sep-2024; returns of 844 people on 8-Sep-2024 and about 1,600 in Sep-2025. [The New Humanitarian](https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/news-feature/2024/07/15/colombia-conflict-displacement-crisis-comes-capital); [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2025/09/08/inicio-el-retorno-de-1600-indigenas-embera-que-llegaron-desplazados-a-bogota/)
column7: Little studied (not in economics). Gómez-Ruiz, Espiga (year nv); ESAP thesis.
column8: Are returns with transfers sustainable, and what happens to returned children's schooling and nutrition? Staggered phases and destinations, 2024 vs. 2025 waves, using District/SDIS censuses (petition), RUV, SIMAT and Banco Agrario payments.

column5: Cuban migrants stranded in Turbo (Colombia, May–Aug 2016; Urabá, Antioquia)
column6: Public calamity declared; about 1,540 "voluntary deportation" requests; crisis closed Aug-2016 after Panama closure in May. [Semana](https://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/uraba-500-inmigrantes-no-han-podido-pasar-a-panama/474790); [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.co/colombia/2016/08/10/colombia-considera-superada-crisis-con-migrantes-cubanos/)
column7: Not studied in economics. Valderrama Espinosa, media analysis (USTA).
column8: Does a transitory transit-migrant shock raise local prices, lodging activity and human smuggling? Turbo vs. rest of Urabá around May-2016 Panama closure and abrupt Aug-2016 end, using Migración Colombia and ICA tax data in FUT/CHIP (no municipal CPI).

column5: Schengen visa waiver for Colombians (Colombia, Dec 2015 onward; EU-bound migration)
column6: Exemption from 3-Dec-2015; 300+ Colombians left for Europe on day one; EU asylum claims by Colombians up 200%+ since 2024 per Frontex. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2015/12/04/mas-de-300-colombianos-salen-hacia-europa-durante-el-primer-dia-sin-visa/); [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/economia/alemania-y-polonia-plantean-pedirle-visa-a-colombianos-920296)
column7: Little studied (provisional). Only EU documents (EUAA Asylum Report 2020).
column8: Did the waiver raise emigration and asylum claims by Colombians? Dec-2015 date, combinable with EV-27 in a three-event design (Venezuelans with Colombian passports confound), using public Eurostat and Migración Colombia data.

column5: Mercury ban in gold mining (Colombia, Jul 2018 onward; gold municipalities such as Segovia and Remedios)
column6: Ban effective 16-Jul-2018 under Law 1658/2013; most mining is informal (weak first stage). [Mongabay](https://news.mongabay.com/2018/08/colombia-bans-the-use-of-mercury-in-mining/); [Colombia Reports](https://colombiareports.com/colombia-imposes-ban-on-mercury-in-gold-mining/amp)
column7: Little studied (mining studied, ban not). Romero and Saavedra (2016) on mining, not the ban.
column8: Did the ban reduce prenatal mercury exposure and improve birth outcomes? Pre/post Jul-2018 × prior municipal mercury/alluvial mining intensity, using public vital statistics, UNODC/SIMCI and ANM data, and SIVIGILA poisonings.

column5: Rotating water rationing (Colombia, Apr 2024–Apr 2025; Bogotá)
column6: 24-hour cuts by zone from 11-Apr-2024, tightened 29-Sep-2024, lifted Apr-2025. [Vanguardia](https://www.vanguardia.com/colombia/2024/04/26/confirmado-bogota-continuara-con-racionamiento-de-agua-de-24-horas-hasta-nueva-orden/); [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/bogota/2024/05/21/tomar-agua-de-la-llave-en-bogota-lo-puede-enfermar-del-estomago-esto-dice-la-secretaria-de-salud/)
column7: Not studied. Only a UNAD working paper on consumption (author nv).
column8: Did cuts raise diarrhea, skin infection or hepatitis A visits among under-5s, varying with household storage (stratum)? Zone × day rotation calendar with placebo Sabana municipalities, using SIVIGILA/SaluData, RIPS and public calendars.

column5: Pertussis outbreak (Colombia, 2025; Bogotá)
column6: From 11 confirmed cases in 2024 to 107 by mid-Apr-2025; by epi-week 38, 2,257 of the country's 2,486 probable cases; 4 infant deaths; maternal Tdap coverage 70–74%. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/colombia/2025/04/15/cuales-son-los-sintomas-de-la-tosferina-bogota-reporta-107-casos/); [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.co/bogota/2025/05/13/bogota-reporta-aumento-de-casos-y-muertes-por-tosferina-distrito-recomienda-vacunacion-en-bebes-y-gestantes/)
column7: Not studied. Only descriptive District Epidemiological Bulletin (author/year nv).
column8: How much does maternal Tdap protect infants from hospitalization or death in a real outbreak? Pre-outbreak Tdap coverage by insurer or locality, test-negative design, birth cohorts around campaigns, using SIVIGILA event 800, PAIWEB and vital statistics.

column5: Family Commissioner offices (Comisarías de Familia) reform (Colombia, Aug 2021–Aug 2023; nationwide)
column6: Law 2126 of 4-Aug-2021 with deadline 4-Aug-2023; by May-2023 only 402 of 1,104 municipalities had full teams. [Procuraduría Directive 0017/2023](https://normograma.com/keralty/compilacion/docs/directiva_procuraduria_0017_2023.htm); [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/atlantico/barranquilla/2026/05/03/comisarias-de-familia-en-el-atlantico-piden-mas-recursos-para-atender-a-la-poblacion/)
column7: Little studied. IDB/Econometría (2014) on a different intervention (Medellín training).
column8: Did completing commission teams raise reports and protection orders and reduce severe violence against children? Staggered municipal compliance dates and municipal category (possible RD; nv), using Medicina Legal and Police open data, SIVIGILA event 875.

column5: Fertility rebound then collapse (Egypt, 2008-2025)
column6: DHS TFR 3.0 (2008) → 3.5 (2014); EFHS 2021 2.85; preliminary EFHS 2025 2.33 with the same method, a fall of about 1.2 children in 11 years. [Radovich et al. 2018](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5773010/); [Ahram Online](https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/577338.aspx)
column7: Partial causal: Krafft 2020 (J. Population Economics) finds falling female public employment "unlikely the main cause"; the 2014-2025 fall has no academic study
column8: Test whether parity-capped Takaful & Karama transfers (nv) and the 2016 and 2022-24 devaluations drove the fall, using governorate food inflation and marriage cohorts in ELMPS 1998-2023 and EDHS/EFHS.

column5: Fertility rebound against the global trend (Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, 2017-2023)
column6: Uzbekistan TFR (WDI) 2.57 (2017) → 3.50 (2023); births 734,100 (2015) → 962,000 (2023); the Kazakh rise spans all birth orders and both ethnic groups, with no tempo effect. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/SPDYNTFRTINUZB); [Kan 2023](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10344851/)
column7: Descriptive: Spoorenberg 2015 (growth explains ~81% of Kazakhstan's 2000-2011 rise); "no consensus on the cause"
column8: Separate a denominator artefact (unregistered female emigration to Russia) from post-2016 reforms and remittances, using district exposure to Russian remittances, Kazakh child-subsidy discontinuities, register vs MICS/DHS birth histories and the 2023 Uzbek census.

column5: Collapse to ultra-low fertility, driven by teens (Chile, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, 2014-2025)
column6: Chile TFR 0.99 (2025, provisional); Costa Rica 1.78 (2014) → 1.12 (2024); Argentina 2.3 → 1.23 (2014-2024), teen fertility −64% vs 2005; 49-85% of the 2011-2020 fall is in the youngest groups. [Bloomberg Línea](https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/chile/chile-registro-la-tasa-de-fecundidad-mas-baja-de-su-historia-en-2025-claves-del-informe-de-ine/); [PRPR](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11113-024-09934-y)
column7: Partial causal: Ceni et al. 2021 (implants explain ~1/3 of Uruguay's fall in public hospitals)
column8: Test LARC diffusion and union formation against a common shock, using Argentina's ENIA provincial rollout (2017) and shutdown (2024), Uruguay's hospital implant timing and Chilean births by maternal nationality in DEIS, MSP and INEC vital records.

column5: Stalled fertility and richest-quintile rebound (Pakistan, 2006-2025)
column6: TFR 3.7 (HIES 2018-19) → 3.6 (2024-25); richest quintile 1.9 → 2.3; fertility rises among women with secondary schooling; "no significant improvement since 2006". [PIDE KB 157](https://file.pide.org.pk/pdfpideresearch/kb-157-stalled-transitions-constrained-choices.pdf); [Dawn](https://www.dawn.com/news/1960651)
column7: Descriptive: Bongaarts and Sathar (family-planning supply, unmet need); richest-quintile rebound: None
column8: Test whether the rich-quintile rebound is an HIES artefact or remittance-driven composition, comparing PDHS birth histories with HIES and using the 2010 devolution of Lady Health Worker funding and district remittance flows (BEOE).

column5: Fertility collapse with more births to girls 10-14 (Philippines, 2017-2024)
column6: NDHS TFR 2.7 (2017) → 1.9 (2022) while modern contraception rose only 40% → 42%; registered births −22.1% (2015-2024); births to mothers aged 10-14: 2,411 (2019) → 3,343 (2023). [PSA](https://psa.gov.ph/content/total-fertility-rate-declined-27-2017-19-2022); [GMA](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/933978/over-3k-children-born-to-mothers-aged-10-14-years-old-in-2023-psa-study/story)
column7: Descriptive: Abrigo and Estopace (PIDS DP 2023-19), 50 years of NDHS, does not isolate the break
column8: Test marital composition, OFW migration and lockdowns against an NDHS 2022 design artefact, using LGU contraceptive spending, quarantine intensity, provincial OFW exposure and a DiD around RA 11648 (nv), with NDHS, PSA civil registry and the 2020 census.

column5: Stalled then reversing transition with rising teen fertility (Bangladesh, 2011-2025)
column6: TFR 2.3 (MICS 2012-13 and 2019) → 2.4 (MICS 2025); teen fertility 83 → 92 per 1,000; contraception 58.2% and falling; marriage before 18: 51.4% (2019) → 47.2% (2025). [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/en/reports/bangladesh-multiple-indicator-cluster-survey-2025); [Dhaka Tribune](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/396843/unfpa-urges-faster-action-as-new-mics-data-shows)
column7: Partial causal: Heath and Mobarak 2015 (garment factories delay marriage; explains the level, not the stall)
column8: Test whether the garment-job plateau and defeminization after ~2013-15 and Gulf male migration raised teen fertility, using upazila distance to factories × post-2015 female factory jobs and district Gulf demand shocks (BMET) with BDHS (GPS) and MICS.

column5: Abrupt fertility fall with less contraception (Jordan, 2012-2017)
column6: TFR ~3.8 from 1998 to 2012, then 3.3 (JLMPS 2016) → 2.6 (JPFHS 2017/18); contraception among married women 61% → 53%; ideal family size fell less than fertility. [Krafft, Kula and Sieverding 2021](https://www.demographic-research.org/volumes/vol45/19/)
column7: Descriptive: Krafft et al. 2021 conclude that "no proximate determinant identifies a clear driver"
column8: Test whether housing and job competition from the 2012-2015 Syrian refugee inflow cut Jordanian fertility, using locality refugee intensity (Fallah, Krafft and Wahba 2019-style design) and JLMPS vs JPFHS birth histories.

column5: Europe's fastest fertility fall despite official pronatalism (Turkey, 2013-2024)
column6: TFR 2.11 (2013) → 1.48 (2024); provinces below replacement 57 (2017) → 71 (2024); Şanlıurfa 3.28 vs Bartın and Eskişehir 1.12. [Turkish Minute](https://turkishminute.com/2025/05/13/turkeys-fertility-fate-hits-record-low-in-2024-deepening-demographic-worries/); [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/turkiye/sanliurfa-tops-fertility-rate-nationwide-trends-show-decline/news)
column7: Descriptive: Greulich, Dasre and Inan 2015 (fewer third-birth transitions; predates the acceleration)
column8: Separate tempo from quantum and the housing channel, using provincial house prices × first births and a birth-date discontinuity for 12-year compulsory schooling (2012), with TurkStat provincial data and TDHS.

column5: Fertility frozen at 2.6 then falling, with wide provincial spread (Indonesia, 2002-2020)
column6: IDHS TFR 2.6 in 2002-03, 2007 and 2012; 2.4 (2017); 2.18 (2020 Long Form census); Jakarta 1.75 vs NTT 3.4; family-planning field workers down by a third from ~35,000 after decentralization. [BPS](https://www.bps.go.id/en/pressrelease/2023/01/30/2039/results-of-long-form-population-census-2020.html); [Jakarta Post](https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2015/08/19/decentralization-threatens-ri-family-planning-program)
column7: Descriptive: Kumar 2016 (more marital exposure and desired fertility, "not an artefact"), contradicted by Taebenu 2020
column8: Test supply erosion after decentralization using post-2001 district splitting (pemekaran), district family-planning budgets (DAPOER), JKN entry (2014) and village field-worker counts in PODES, with IFLS and IDHS.

column5: Flat fertility, then 2005-2010 plunge, 2014-2020 stall and new fall (Rwanda, 2005-2025)
column6: DHS TFR 6.1 (2005) → 4.6 (2010) → 4.1 (2019-20) → 3.7 (2025); modern contraception 17% → 52% (2005-2010); desired fertility, actual fertility and child mortality fell together. [NISR](https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2026-01/DHS7_booklet_V2.pdf); [PRB](https://scorecard.prb.org/poppov-rwanda-unmet-need/)
column7: Descriptive: World Bank PRWP 6741 decomposes 2005-2010 and leaves an unexplained residual
column8: Test whether land pressure, the staggered 2009-2013 land tenure regularization and imihigo family-planning targets lowered desired fertility, using sector-level regularization timing and district targets with DHS 1992-2025 (GPS) and EICV.

column5: Fertility roller coaster (1.9 → 2.4 → 1.3?) with low female participation (Sri Lanka, 2000-2024)
column6: TFR 1.9 (DHS 2000) → 2.4 (2012 census) as age at marriage fell to 23.4; births 301,706 (2020) → 220,761 (2024); disputed 2024 census TFR of 1.3; FLFP ~31-32% (2022-2025). [Cambridge JBS](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-biosocial-science/article/fertility-transition-in-sri-lanka-is-it-a-temporary-phenomenon/8A64BDEFC2A7EF022C26CA55FBB68937); [Daily Mirror](https://www.dailymirror.lk/breaking-news/Sri-Lankas-Fertility-Shock-Is-the-Crisis-Real/108-339813)
column7: Descriptive: Wijesekere and Arunachalam 2015 (the 2000 figure may be wrong); the post-2022 collapse is Speculation
column8: Separate tempo, selective emigration and census undercount after the 2022 crisis using monthly district birth registrations × inflation × SLBFE departures, and test the rebound with tsunami-hit coastal districts and the post-2009 North and East.

column5: Extreme desired fertility that barely moves (Niger and northern Nigeria, 2003-2024)
column6: Nigeria TFR 4.8 (NDHS 2023-24): Northeast 6.1 vs South-South 3.3; desired family size 7.5 in the Northwest (2018); Niger mean ideal 10.2 children, TFR 7.0 (2006) → 7.6 (2012), modern contraception 12% → 10% (2012-2021). [DHS PR157](https://dhsprogram.com/pubs/pdf/PR157/PR157.pdf); [BMC Women's Health](https://bmcwomenshealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12905-019-0747-9/tables/2)
column7: Descriptive: pronatalist norms, religion, polygamy and low empowerment (BMC Women's Health 2019)
column8: Test land abundance, co-wife competition and insecurity by comparing Hausa communities across the Niger-Nigeria border, cohorts exposed to sharia penal codes in 12 states (1999-2001) and ACLED conflict exposure, with DHS, ENAFEME 2021 and MICS.

column5: Ultra-low fertility at middle income and accelerating birth decline (Thailand, 2019-2024)
column6: 462,240 births in 2024, the first year below 500,000 since 1949; deaths exceed births for the fourth year; TFR 1.0-1.21 depending on source; never-married women aged 15-49 at 9% (2018). [Khaosod](https://www.khaosodenglish.com/news/2025/01/17/thailands-population-drops-below-66-million-as-births-hit-75-year-low/); [Nation Thailand](https://nationthailand.com/thailand/general/40036208)
column7: Descriptive: NIDA (singlehood driven by educational composition); no causal studies
column8: Test household debt (nv) and migration-driven grandparent households using provincial tourism exposure during COVID and farm-debt programmes, with DOPA provincial births, MICS 2012-2022 and comparisons with Vietnam and Malaysia.

column5: Algeria's rebound above 3 while Tunisia falls to ~1.5 (Algeria vs Tunisia, 2010-2024)
column6: Algeria above 3 in the mid-2010s, falling since 2017 to 2.61 (2024); Tunisia ~1.53 (2024) with female age at marriage 28.9; Morocco 1.97 with no rebound. [INED](https://www.ined.fr/fr/publications/editions/population-et-societes/fecondite-historiquement-basse-au-maghreb); [INED](https://www.ined.fr/en/press/maghreb-region-fertility-has-reached-historically-low-levels)
column7: Descriptive: INED 2026 (marriage boom from a temporary economic upturn and large cohorts)
column8: Test whether oil-funded subsidized housing (AADL) and youth credit cheapened marriage, using AADL allocations by wilaya-year × marriages and births and the post-2014 oil-price fall, with ONS vital statistics and MICS Algeria.

column5: Sex ratio at birth normalizes in Georgia but not Azerbaijan (Georgia vs Azerbaijan, 2009-2023)
column6: Georgia SRB 110 (2009) → 105 (2016), with a significant fall after 2014 in all regions and birth orders; Azerbaijan ~114.7 (2001) → ~111.6 (2023); son preference in Georgia −15 pp (2010-2019). [ISET-PI](https://iset-pi.ge/en/blog/108-has-georgia-solved-its-missing-girls-problem); [UNFPA](https://azerbaijan.unfpa.org/en/node/46216)
column7: Descriptive: Duthé et al. 2012 (modern technology for "old desires"); Otarashvili pre/post abortion policies
column8: Build a synthetic control of Georgia vs Azerbaijan and compare Azeri minorities in Kvemo Kartli (same law, different culture) to test the 2014 abortion regulation (nv) and female emigration to the EU, using Geostat registry, Caucasus Barometer and MICS 2018.

column5: Late SRB rise, plateau at ~111-112 and North-South divergence (Vietnam, 2005-2024)
column6: SRB 110.7 in 2024 (GSO); in 2021-2024, 10 of 11 Red River Delta provinces exceed 110 and some localities near 120, while the South is at 105-108; levels off at ~112-113 around 2014. [VietnamNet](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/vietnam-faces-growing-birth-gender-gap-hanoi-leads-imbalance-2398513.html); [Tuoi Tre](https://news.tuoitre.vn/120-boys-per-100-girls-gender-imbalance-remains-critical-in-vietnam-103250426175958467.htm)
column7: Descriptive: Guilmoto 2012; Becquet and Guilmoto 2018 (patrilineal kinship, technology, low fertility); no evaluation of sex-disclosure bans
column8: Test land-inheritance incentives in the Delta using the 2013 and 2024 Land Laws × provincial land tenure and the end of the two-child limit (2025, nv), with IPUMS 1999/2009/2019, GSO population surveys and MICS.

column5: Low upper-secondary completion in a high-income country, then a jump (Uruguay, 2006-2023)
column6: Completion at ages 21-23: 42.7% (2019), +10.5 pp since 2006; 43.3% → 50.9% (2022); 51.6% (2023), "one of the worst positions in LAC". [El Observador](https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/anep-incumplio-tres-de-las-cuatro-metas-de-egreso-fijadas-para-liceales-en-2018-2019811470); [Montevideo Portal](https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Noticias/Sube-porcentaje-de-jovenes-que-terminan-bachillerato-paso-de-43-3-a-50-9-en-tres-anos-uc872595)
column7: Partial causal: Menese Camargo 2021 (Asignaciones Familiares-Plan de Equidad: positive in lower secondary, null or negative in upper)
column8: Test whether returns to early work in the 2004-2014 commodity boom and the 2023 promotion rules drove completion, using departmental commodity-price shift-share and cohort discontinuities by regulation, with ECH 2006-2024 and ANEP trajectories.

column5: PISA scores far above income level, then a sharp 2022 drop (Vietnam, 2012-2022)
column6: After correcting for selection Vietnam remains a large outlier; observables explain at most ~30%; PISA 2022: 469 maths, 462 reading, 472 science, down 27, 43 and 71 points from 2018. [RISE WP-036](https://riseprogramme.org/sites/default/files/2020-11/RISE_WP-036_Dang_Glewwe_Lee_Vu.pdf); [Dan Tri](https://dtinews.dantri.com.vn/print/20231208100756153.htm)
column7: Partial causal: Dang, Glewwe, Lee and Vu 2023 (EER), selection does not close the gap; the 2022 drop is Speculation
column8: Test centralized teacher accountability, private tutoring and dynamic selection using the staggered provincial rollout of the 2018 GDPT curriculum, provincial secondary enrolment 2012-2022 and PISA item response times, with Young Lives.

column5: Persistent reversed gender gap in schooling despite the mining collapse (Lesotho, Botswana, Namibia, Eswatini, South Africa, 2001-2024)
column6: In Lesotho 90% of girls reach grade 7 vs 66% of boys; 76 boys per 100 girls in lower secondary (2019); Lesotho's most educated women have the highest unemployment. [World Bank](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/africacan/education-employment-paradox-lesotho-afe-0124); [Nation.africa](https://nation.africa/kenya/news/gender/why-lesotho-s-most-educated-women-still-face-the-highest-unemployment-rates--5546634)
column7: Descriptive: Pitikoe 2016 (boys herding from ages 3-5); male mine migration and masculinity norms
column8: Test herding and mine-migration channels using the collapse of TEBA mine recruitment by district × birth cohort, livestock, wool and mohair prices, and droughts × herd ownership, with IPUMS-I and Lesotho DHS.

column5: Boys falling behind in schooling in poor countries (Sahel and Southeast Asia, to 2025)
column6: UNESCO 2022: boys already lag in Burkina Faso, Burundi, Gambia, Rwanda and Senegal; Cambodian girls outpace boys in upper secondary; in Indonesia and Fiji boys spend 3 fewer hours on education because they play more, not work more. [UKFIET](https://www.ukfiet.org/2022/launch-of-the-global-report-on-boys-disengagement-from-education/); [Monash](https://www.monash.edu/business/che/impact-and-engagement/research-bites/gender-gap-in-childrens-education-in-informal-settlements)
column7: Descriptive: Okabe 2025 (sex-differentiated returns); opportunity-cost story contradicted by Monash
column8: Date the reversal by country and region with IPUMS × productive structure, and test girl-targeted scholarships and construction or mining booms × male enrolment, using UIS, DHS/MICS by cohort and sex, and time-use data.

column5: Women far ahead in education but not in the labour market (Jamaica, Barbados, Trinidad and Tobago, 2009-2026)
column6: Female/male tertiary ratio: Barbados 1.55 (2011), Jamaica 1.43 (2015); female CSEC advantage in all subjects and SES groups (2016-2020); Jamaica has the world's highest share of female managers (ILO 2015) yet lower female pay. [IDB 2024](https://www.iadb.org/en/gender-gaps-education-caribbean-are-girls-doing-better-boys); [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:fiu:wpaper:2410)
column7: Descriptive: Wright (FIU WP 2410), up to 78% of Jamaica's pass gap explained by school and subject choice
column8: Test differential returns to credentials using RDD from exam-based secondary assignment (GSAT/PEP in Jamaica, SEA in Trinidad) by sex, parish homicides and male demand shocks (construction, bauxite), with CXC/CSEC, JSLC and LFS.

column5: Rising out-of-school numbers after Universal Basic Education (Nigeria, 2004-2024)
column6: Primary-age out-of-school 6.4 million (2000) → 9.6 million (2020); 10.2 million of 18.3 million (UNICEF 2024); net attendance 61% (2008) → 68.7% (2014), Northwest 50.5%, Northeast 42.5% (year nv). [GEM blog](https://world-education-blog.org/2022/09/02/nigeria-has-more-children-out-of-school-than-any-other-country-why/); [Dataphyte](https://dataphyte.com/investigation/2020/08/a-review-of-the-basic-education-situation-in-nigeria)
column7: Partial causal for the Northeast only (Boko Haram and kidnappings); otherwise Descriptive (population growth, GEM)
column8: Estimate UBE effects using unclaimed UBEC matching funds by state-year × school-age cohorts and LGA kidnapping exposure (ACLED), with NDHS 2003-2023-24, MICS, NEDS and GHS-Panel.

column5: Double male disadvantage in tertiary education and life expectancy (Mongolia, 2001-2024)
column6: Female/male tertiary ratio 1.41 (2024); life-expectancy gap 4.19 years (1992) → 9.67 (2018, NSO), 9.4 (World Bank, 2024); men smoke 13 times more; boys were 66% of dropouts in 2015-16. Share of widening after 2001: nv. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/SEENRTERTFMZSMNG); [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/23/mongolia-s-commitment-to-gender-equality-a-path-to-national-development-vision)
column7: Partial causal for alcohol and tobacco; education gap called "well explored" (Graduate Institute)
column8: Test marriage-market hypergamy and the mining boom as a male opportunity cost using dzud shocks (2009-10, 2023-24) by soum and the 2010-2013 mining boom by aimag, with the livestock census, HSES, MICS and IPUMS.

column5: Female LFP nearly doubles in PLFS, partly via survey instructions (India, with Bangladesh parallel, 2017-2024)
column6: PLFS FLFPR 15+: 23.3% (2017-18) → 41.7% (2023-24); rural 47.6%, +6 pp in one year; 67% of women workers self-employed. Bangladesh rural 50.89% but urban 31% → 23.6%. [MoSPI](https://mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_AR_PLFS_2023_24_22092024.pdf); [Daily Star](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/rural-bangladesh-women-labour-force-the-rise-3302001)
column7: Descriptive/Partial causal: Thakur and Chaudhary 2025 (IJLE) on revised 2023-24 field instructions; Bangladesh: Speculation
column8: Separate instruction effects from behaviour using FSU and enumerator variation before and after the 2023-24 instruction change and the urban rotation panel, benchmarked against TUS 2019 vs 2024, CPHS and district Jal Jeevan Mission rollout.

column5: ~33% unemployment with a "missing" informal sector (South Africa, 2001-2025)
column6: Unemployment 33.2% (Q2 2025); informal workers ~33% of 17.1 million employed (Q4 2025) vs 85.8% informality across Africa; series break from Q3 2025 (21st ICLS). [Stats SA](https://www.statssa.gov.za/publications/P0211/Presentation%20QLFS%20Q2%202025.pdf); [Stats SA](https://www.statssa.gov.za/?p=19240)
column7: Descriptive/Partial causal: Kingdon and Knight 2001/2004 (entry barriers, involuntary unemployment)
column8: Separate entry costs, supermarket competition, crime and reservation wages using staggered supermarket entry into townships, municipal street-trading bylaws and the 2020 R350 SRD grant as a non-labour income shock, with the QLFS panel, NIDS and SA-TIED.

column5: Female LFP stalls at ~50-52% while fertility drops below replacement (Latin America, 2000-2024)
column6: Significant slowdown in the 2000s in 15 countries ends a 50-year trend; FLFP 51.8% (2019), 52.1% (Q2 2024) vs 74.3% for men; regional TFR 1.8 (2024), below replacement since 2015. [CEDLAS](https://www.cedlas.econo.unlp.edu.ar/wp/en/?p=3952); [Bloomberg Línea](https://bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/participacion-laboral-en-america-latina-bolivia-y-peru-lideran-segun-la-oit/)
column7: Descriptive: Gasparini and Marchionni 2015/2017 (income effect of the 2003-2013 boom)
column8: Use Uruguay's implants and Argentina's ENIA as instruments for young women's labour supply and contrast abrupt (Chile, Costa Rica) vs gradual fertility falls with shift-share by age, education and marital status, using SEDLAC, IPUMS-I and national household surveys.

column5: Female LFP flat at ~51% for two decades, then a recent rise (Indonesia, 2000-2025)
column6: ~51% for two decades as norms progress but structural change offsets them; 54.03% (2021) → 56.63% (Aug 2025) vs 84.40% for men. [RePEc](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:taf:bindes:v:55:y:2019:i:2:p:157-192); [CNBC Indonesia](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/lifestyle/20260505154431-33-732479/ketimpangan-gender-membaik-tapi-wanita-ri-masih-sulit-di-dunia-kerja)
column7: Descriptive: Cameron, Contreras Suárez and Rowell 2019 (BIES); post-2021 rise: None
column8: Test childcare, piety and platform work using village preschool (PAUD) expansion in PODES, district 4G rollout and religious bylaws, with Sakernas, IFLS and SUSENAS.

column5: Female LFP falls as schooling rises; inactivity grows among tertiary-educated women (Morocco, 1999-2025)
column6: FLFP 30.4% (1999) → 19% (2025) vs 68.5% for men; school enrolment at 15-17: 46.3% (2010) → 70.9% (2020); inactivity of tertiary-educated women rising from 13% in 2010. [Hespress](https://fr.hespress.com/481129-481129.html); [World Bank 2021](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/269721616435662650/pdf/Trends-and-Determinants-of-Female-Labor-Force-Participation-in-Morocco-An-Initial-Exploratory-Analysis.pdf)
column7: Descriptive/Partial causal: Verme, Barry and Guennouni 2016 (marriage, household income, low job-intensity growth)
column8: Test public-hiring caps and mobility in public space using graduate cohorts before and after caps on public-sector hiring and the Rabat (2011) and Casablanca (2012) tram lines by neighbourhood, with ENE, MHYS 2009-10 and the ONDH panel.

column5: 22 years of stagnation without war, with cyclical political crises (Madagascar, 2002-2024)
column6: GDP per capita (2015 USD) ~US$407 (2002) → ~US$456 (2024), about +12% in 22 years; political crises in 2001-02 and 2009-2013. [Trading Economics](https://it.tradingeconomics.com/madagascar/gdp-per-capita); [K4D-IDS](https://k4d.ids.ac.uk/?p=1382)
column7: Descriptive: Razafindrakoto, Roubaud and Wachsberger 2020 (political economy of recurrent crises)
column8: Test rice-productivity stagnation and trade-access channels using the 2010-2014 AGOA suspension × export-processing-zone exposure and regional rice yields × climate, with 1-2-3/ENEMPSI surveys, EPM and DHS.

column5: Maternal mortality rises despite near-universal hospital delivery (Dominican Republic; also Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela; 2000-2024)
column6: Modelled MMR 79 (2000) → 107 (2020); surveillance 127.7 (2024); skilled delivery "near 100%"; cesareans 31% (2002) → 58% (2014); Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela also have skilled attendance ≥96% and MMR >120. [World Bank Gender Data Portal](https://genderdata.worldbank.org/data/download/pdfs/countries/dominican-republic.pdf); [PAHO via ecoi.net](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2121829.html); [OECD Panorama 2020](https://oecd.org/es/publications/panorama-de-la-salud-latinoamerica-y-el-caribe-2020_740f9640-es/full-report/component-15)
column7: Descriptive: Miller et al. 2003 ("paradox of the DR", quality of institutional care); De Jesus et al. 2023
column8: Separate better registration, composition and clinical practice using cause-specific deaths × hospital cesarean rates, staggered SINAVE rollout by province, SeNaSa payment rules and maternal-nationality shift-share, with ENDESA/ENHOGAR-MICS sibling modules and MoH hospital bulletins.
column9: Rompecabezas en países en desarrollo; Public health puzzles

column5: Cesarean becomes the majority mode of delivery in middle-income countries (Egypt, Turkey, Brazil, Dominican Republic, 2000-2025)
column6: LAC 42.8% vs world 21.1%; WHO: cesareans exceed vaginal births in the DR, Brazil, Cyprus, Egypt and Turkey; Egypt ~10% (2000) → 72% (2021); Turkey 60.5% (2022); Brazil 55.4% → 57.2% (2016-2020), rising in North/Northeast, falling in Southeast. [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34130991/); [WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/16-06-2021-Caesarean-Section-Rates-Continue-To-Rise-Amid-Growing-Inequalities-In-Access); [Egyptian Streets](https://egyptianstreets.com/2025/10/22/whats-fueling-egypts-rise-in-cesarean-deliveries/)
column7: Partial causal: Parto Adequado evaluation in Brazil (CSP 2024); maternal demand in Egypt (Jauniaux et al.) Descriptive; cross-country: None
column8: Test supply incentives vs norms using weekday and holiday birth spikes and Robson groups by hospital, staggered Parto Adequado entry, Turkey's 2012 law (nv), ANS Res. 368 (nv) and Egypt's 2025 Robson mandate, with SINASC and DHS for Egypt, Turkey and the DR.
column9: Rompecabezas en países en desarrollo; Public health puzzles

column4: Preterm birth and low birth weight
column5: Preterm birth flat and low birth weight barely falling despite better maternal health (global LMICs, 2000-2020)
column6: LBW 16.6% (2000) → 14.7% (2020), falling ~0.3% a year since 2012; 13.4 million preterm births in 2020, rates static in 2010-2020 (global 9.8% → 9.9%). [OUCI record](https://ouci.dntb.gov.ua/works/45dzVxE7); [WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/06-10-2023-1-in-10-babies-worldwide-are-born-early--with-major-impacts-on-health-and-survival); [LSHTM](https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/4667148)
column7: Descriptive: Okwaraji et al. (Lancet 2024); Ohuma et al. (Lancet 2023); cesarean-to-preterm link: Speculation
column8: Test whether scheduled cesareans and inductions before 39 weeks, heat and maternal metabolic risk offset gains, using gestational-week distributions × hospital cesarean rates, ERA5 heatwaves by gestation date and cesarean payment reforms (Brazil, Turkey), with SINASC, DEIS Chile and INEGI.
column9: Rompecabezas en países en desarrollo; Public health puzzles

column5: Neonatal mortality stalls amid a facility-birth boom; stillbirth progress slows (Bangladesh, 2014-2024)
column6: BDHS neonatal mortality 28 (2014) → 30 (2017-18) while under-5 mortality fell 43 → 31 (2017-22); global neonatal share of under-5 deaths 41% (2000) → 47% (2022); stillbirth decline slowed 53% after 2015. [Prothom Alo](https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/Infant-mortality-rate-not-decreasing); [UNB](https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/under-5-mortality-rate-marks-sharp-fall-in-bangladesh-report/113572)
column7: Descriptive: intrapartum-quality consensus; Sci Reports 2024 (poverty and schooling)
column8: Test stillbirth-to-neonatal reclassification vs low-quality private clinics by comparing perinatal mortality (invariant to reclassification) with neonatal mortality and stillbirths in pooled BDHS 1993-2022 birth histories, SVRS and MICS 2019.

column5: Infant mortality turns up around 2009, before the economic collapse (Venezuela, 2008-2016)
column6: IMR 15.0 (2008) → 21.1 (2016); "around 2009 the long-term decline stopped", during an oil boom with Barrio Adentro; 2016 infant deaths +30.12% to 11,466, maternal deaths up ~65%. [PubMed 30686723](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30686723/); [VOA](https://www.voanews.com/amp/venezuela-health-data-soaring-infant-mortality-malaria/3845006.html)
column7: Descriptive/Partial causal for 2014 onward (economic collapse); 2009 inflection: None
column8: Test hospital decay masked by primary-care missions, the 2009-10 electricity crisis and dengue, or an indirect-estimation artefact, using the death registry by cause and state timing (INE to ~2014, WHO Mortality DB) and Brazil's SINASC by maternal nationality.

column5: Child and women's anaemia rise while determinants improve, then NFHS-6 drops the indicator (India, 2015-2026)
column6: Children 6-59 months 58.6% → 67.1% and women 53.1% → 57.0% (NFHS-4 → 5) despite better IFA, WASH and schooling; capillary 59.2% vs venous 35.2%; NFHS-6 (2026) dropped all 7 anaemia indicators. [Down To Earth](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/news/health/anaemia-in-women-and-children-on-the-rise-assam-fares-worst-nfhs-5-80357); [Indian Pediatrics](https://indianpediatrics.net/nov2022/837.pdf); [The Wire](https://thewire.in/health/nfhs-key-indicators-missing-government-clarifies)
column7: Partial causal for the level only: capillary-blood bias (Indian Pediatrics 2022; Kurpad 2025); the rise: Descriptive (BMC Public Health 2023 decomposition)
column8: Test round-specific measurement (devices, teams, COVID-split fieldwork) against real change using NFHS-5 Phase 1 vs Phase 2, team fixed effects, men's anaemia as a placebo, the CNNS venous benchmark and district fortified-rice rollout.
column9: Rompecabezas en países en desarrollo; Public health puzzles

column5: Wasting and underweight flat while stunting falls and GDP grows (India, 2000-2026)
column6: Wasting 17.1% (1998-02) → 21% (2012-16) while other indices fell; NFHS-6: stunting 35.5% → 29.3% but wasting 19.3% → 19.0% and underweight 32.1% → 31.8%. [The Secretariat](https://thesecretariat.in/article/india-s-nutrition-enigma-growing-economy-malnourished-children); [Outlook](https://www.outlookindia.com/national/indias-double-burden-malnutrition-declines-as-obesity-and-diabetes-climb)
