column7: Partial causal: Subramanyam et al. 2011 (no strong growth effect); stunting vs underweight divergence: None
column8: Test anthropometric measurement error against heat and maternal thinness using WHZ dispersion and age heaping by field agency, inter-agency variation within states and temperature shocks linked to NFHS geocodes, with NFHS-1 to 6 and CNNS.
column9: Rompecabezas en países en desarrollo; Public health puzzles

column5: Adult height falls between NFHS-3 and NFHS-4 (India, 2005-2016)
column6: Men aged 15-25 lost 1.10 cm and men 26-50 lost 0.86 cm; poor women −0.57 cm; Scheduled Tribes −0.42 cm; part of the analysis covers only 11 states. [PMC8448320](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8448320/); [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/health/indians-got-shorter-over-last-decade-trends-in-st-women-need-urgent-attention-jnu-study-says/741857)
column7: Speculation/Descriptive: Choudhary, Das and Ghodajkar 2021 (PLOS ONE); nutrition and inequality
column8: Test measurement error or a different male subsample in NFHS-3 against a real decline in new cohorts by tracking height by birth cohort (not age group) across NFHS-3/4/5 and the IHDS panel.

column5: Rural BMI rises faster than urban BMI (LMICs, 1985-2017)
column6: Over 55% of the global rise in mean BMI came from rural areas, over 80% in some LMIC regions (2,009 studies, 112 million adults); rural +2.1 kg/m² vs urban +1.3 (women); exception: sub-Saharan African women. [UPF repository](https://repositori.upf.edu/items/d0d0ac9e-2f66-4f5d-9f18-97fcdd0ea281); [LIH](https://events.lih.lu/blog/our-news-1/post/global-burden-study-obesity-rising-faster-in-rural-areas-than-in-cities-253) (nv)
column7: Speculation/Descriptive: NCD-RisC authors (rural incomes, mechanisation, cars, processed food)
column8: Test road-led ultra-processed food distribution, mechanisation and cash transfers using rural road paving (PMGSY, Vías Terciarias), distributor or supermarket entry and CCT phase-ins, with DHS/NFHS anthropometrics (GPS), ENSANUT and SHRUG.

column5: Diabetes mortality far above peers with similar obesity (Mexico, 1998-2024)
column6: Diabetes mortality 43.4 → 80.1 per 100k (1998-2018); years of life lost per person 1.13 in Mexico vs 0.18 in Chile (2000-11); 112,577 deaths, ~13.7% of all deaths, in 2024. [PMC8522739](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8522739/); [Gaceta Sanitaria 2015](https://scielosp.org/pdf/gs/2015.v29n3/172-177/es)
column7: Partial causal (simulation): Palloni and Beltrán-Sánchez 2015 (obesity to diabetes); cross-country gap: Speculation
column8: Separate certification artefacts from care quality using multiple-cause death files for Mexico, Chile and Colombia and event studies of the Seguro Popular rollout (2004-10) and the 2020 INSABI transition, with INEGI deaths and ENSANUT HbA1c.

column5: Hypertension treatment and control flat as HIV care platforms scale up (sub-Saharan Africa, 1990-2019)
column6: Little change in treatment and control in most SSA countries since 1990; treatment below 25% (women) and 20% (men) in some; prevalence "high and increasing". [Southampton](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/451199/1/NCD_RisC_hypertension_paper.docx); [J Hum Hypertens 2024](https://link.springer.com/10.1038/s41371-024-00913-6)
column7: Descriptive: NCD-RisC (Lancet 2021), weak primary care, drug supply, cost; HIV-NCD integration trials (nv)
column8: Test whether HIV earmarks crowded out NCD care using district PEPFAR intensity and timing, essential-medicines-list changes and STEPS and DHS blood-pressure rounds, with PEPFAR site spending and NIDS.

column5: Life-expectancy gains at 65 stall as the cardiovascular decline slows (7 Latin American countries, 2010-2019)
column6: Gains slowed to ~0.5-1 year; the cardiovascular contribution more than halved vs 2000-2010, in seven Latin American countries plus the US and Canada. [MPIDR](https://www.demogr.mpg.de/en/publications_databases_6118/publications_1904/journal_articles/catching_up_with_stagnation_cause_specific_dynamics_of_change_in_life_expectancy_at_age_65_in_the_united_8671)
column7: Descriptive: Bramajo, Mehta and Myrskylä 2025 (Gerontologist)
column8: Test whether metabolic risk (obesity, diabetes) offsets treatment gains by relating cause-specific decompositions by country and region to subnational diabetes prevalence, using national vital statistics (INEGI, DEIS, EEVV) and the WHO Mortality Database.

column5: Rising suicide outlier in the Southern Cone; highest rates in the Americas (Uruguay; Guyana and Suriname, 2000-2025)
column6: Uruguay 23.3 per 100k in 2022 (record) and 19.16 in 2025 vs ~9 in the Americas; 78% men; peaks above 75 and at 25-29; Guyana had the world's highest rate in 2012 (WHO), linked to Indo-Caribbeans and pesticides; rise since 2000 (nv). [MercoPress](https://en.mercopress.com/2022/07/01/uruguay-the-worst-in-the-americas-for-suicides-reached-a-new-record-for-self-murders-in-2021); [infonews/AP](https://infonews.ca/?p=2445277); [Stabroek](https://stabroeknews.com/?p=303508)
column7: Descriptive: Robertt 1999 (Durkheimian anomie); pesticides in Guyana
column8: Test lethal-means access and rural income shocks using departmental agricultural-price shift-share in Uruguay and pesticide bans in Guyana and Suriname (dates nv), checking differential under-registration in neighbours, with MSP and DEIS death records and PAHO data.

column5: Coverage collapse after Seguro Popular, a "recovery" that may be a questionnaire change, and measles return (Mexico, 2018-2026)
column6: Lack of health access 16.2% (2018) → 39.1% (2022, 50.4 million); INEGI 2024: 34.2% after a questionnaire change vs 44.1% on CONEVAL-consistent criteria; OOP 41.2% of health spending; 9,074 measles cases and 28 deaths since Feb 2025. [Expansión](https://politica.expansion.mx/mexico/2023/08/10/coneval-se-duplica-la-poblacion-sin-acceso-a-salud); [México ¿cómo vamos?](https://mexicocomovamos.mx/publicaciones/2025/08/medicion-de-pobreza-2024/); [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/mexico-reports-28-measles-deaths-since-outbreak-in-2025/3827591)
column7: Partial causal: AEA 2025 working paper on repeal and infant mortality (results not seen)
column8: Test whether people lost services or only an insurance label using staggered state adherence to IMSS-Bienestar (2022-24) and pre-reform enrolment intensity, recoding ENIGH 2024 to CONEVAL criteria, with ENSANUT, DGIS open data and SINAVE measles data.

column5: Insurance expansion without out-of-pocket relief (India, Philippines, Indonesia, 2014-2024)
column6: No OOP reduction with PM-JAY in Chhattisgarh nor for deliveries in NFHS-5; Philippines OOP 44.4% of health spending (2023) vs a UHC Act limit of 20%; Indonesia OOP above 30% despite near-universal JKN. [Garg et al. 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7298746); [BusinessWorld](https://www.bworldonline.com/?p=613871); [Maulana et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10021284/)
column7: Descriptive: Garg et al. 2020 (null association)
column8: Test outpatient-drug exclusion and provider balance billing using the SECC-2011 eligibility RD and staggered state PM-JAY adoption (nv), the Konsulta rollout (nv) and Indonesia's PBI threshold, with NSS 75th round, HCES 2022-23, FIES and IFLS.

column5: Childhood vaccination falls from ~2015, before COVID, across all antigens (Brazil, 2012-2021)
column6: Coverage 96.3% (2015) → 83.8% (2017); under-2 series 88.85% (2015) → 62.35% (2021); measles-free in 2016, then 10,346 cases in 2018; MMR1 −17% in the North/Northeast, steeper in deprived municipalities. [PMC8594206](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8594206); [LSHTM](https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/4676004)
column7: Speculation/Descriptive: hesitancy; deprivation (LSHTM, ecological); denominator problems (RESS 2023)
column8: Separate a registry or denominator artefact from a real decline using municipal timing of the SI-PNI nominal-registry switch (nv), the 2022 census denominator revision and Mais Médicos Cuban-exit intensity (2018), with SI-PNI, SINASC and CNES.

column5: Immunization collapses before the Dengvaxia scare (Philippines, 2013-2019)
column6: DTP1 98% (2013) → 69% (2015), with stock-outs; "vaccines important" 93% (2015) → 32% (2018); measles 47,871 cases and 632 deaths in 2019. [HV&I 2020](https://informahealthcare.com/doi/full/10.1080/21645515.2020.1841541); [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/1.4930139); [ReliefWeb](https://m.reliefweb.int/report/3561938/philippines/philippines-measles-outbreak-operation-update-re-emergence-vaccine-preventable?lang=fr)
column7: Descriptive/Partial causal for 2018 onward: Larson/LSHTM on the Dengvaxia confidence shock
column8: Test a 2014-16 procurement failure against an administrative-denominator artefact using antigen- and region-specific timing, admin vs NDHS 2013/2017/2022 card coverage and Dengvaxia school-programme regions as DiD intensity (nv), with FHSIS and WUENIC.

column5: Synchronized syphilis surge; in Brazil maternal detection rises while congenital cases fall (Brazil, Argentina, Chile, 2010-2025)
column6: Argentina 26,647 (2022) → 36,917 (2024) cases, a record; Brazil 2024: ~256,000 acquired (~120 per 100k), 89,000 gestational, 24,000 congenital, congenital falling since 2019; São Paulo gestational 15.4 → 71.4 per 1,000 (2014-24); Chile 19 → 31.4 per 100k (2010-19). [Metrópoles](https://www.metropoles.com/saude/sifilis-avanca-no-brasil-saiba); [SMS-SP](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/documents/d/saude/boletim-epidemiologico-sifilis-2025)
column7: Partial causal: Braga et al. (CID), 2014-17 penicillin shortage multiplied congenital risk 2.23 times in Rio
column8: Separate rapid-test detection from true incidence using staggered rapid-test and Rede Cegonha timing, latent vs primary/secondary ratios, municipal penicillin stockouts, PrEP site openings and the 2017 case-definition break (nv), with SINAN, SINASC, SICLOM and SNVS.

column5: HIV surges against the global decline (Philippines, 2010-2025)
column6: New infections +543% (2010-23), 33% among ages 15-24; ~4,400 (2010) → 29,600 (2024); ~252,800 people living with HIV, ~40% undiagnosed; Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam saw falling incidence. [UNAIDS AP](https://unaids-ap.org/2025/06/04/unaids-calls-for-urgent-action-as-philippines-faces-fastest-growing-hiv-epidemic-in-asia-pacific/); [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/10/24/who-sounds-alarm-over-sharp-increases-in-hiv-cases-in-philippines-fiji-papua-new-guinea)
column7: Descriptive: HRW 2016 (legal barriers such as parental consent and local condom bans)
column8: Test legal and supply barriers for youth and app-mediated network shifts using city ordinances (condom bans vs Quezon City), RA 11166 lowering the testing age to 15 (nv), PrEP and treatment-hub openings and broadband rollout, with HARP, IHBSS and YAFS.

column5: HIV rises in a high-income country with universal ART (Chile, 2010-2022)
column6: Highest percentage rise in new infections in Latin America since 2010; +34% in 2010-18; migrant incidence 22.6 → 115.6 per 100k, and the migrant-to-Chilean ratio 1.0 → 7.6 (2013-22). [UNAIDS 2019](https://www.unaids.org/sites/default/files/media_asset/2019-global-AIDS-update_latin-america_en.pdf); [PMC11759548](https://rcastoragev2.blob.core.windows.net/3d65a77c8a38bdb45f43df4ae080af0f/main.PMC11759548.pdf)
column7: Descriptive: migration; prevention deficits and testing expansion are Speculation
column8: Distinguish infection after arrival (FONASA access frictions) from imported prevalence using CD4 at diagnosis by time since arrival, migration waves across comunas and regularization episodes (nv), with Minsal/ISP microdata and the 2017 census.

column5: TB rises in Latin America while falling globally (Brazil, Peru and others, 2015-2023)
column6: Latin American TB incidence +19% since 2015 vs −8.7% globally; incarceration's 2019 attributable fraction ~36.9% in Brazil and 23.3% in Peru, leaving about two-thirds of the rise unexplained. [MIDAS](https://midasnetwork.us/papers/mass-incarceration-as-a-driver-of-the-tuberculosis-epidemic-in-latin-america-and-projected-effects-of-policy-alternatives-a-mathematical-modelling-study/); [Agência Brasil](https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/saude/noticia/2024-10/encarceramento-e-principal-causa-de-tuberculose-na-america-latina)
column7: Partial causal (model-based): Liu, Andrews et al. 2024 (Lancet Public Health)
column8: Test austerity-driven treatment interruption, diabetes and GeneXpert detection using prison openings and overcrowding spillovers, the 2006 drug law (nv) and GeneXpert rollout (nv), with SINAN-TB, SISDEPEN and Peru's SIGTB.
